Rain Cover Detachable or integrated cover Protects gear from rain and mud
Compression Straps Straps on the sides or front Reduces pack volume, stabilises load
Attachment Points Loops, hooks, or elastic cords Secures additional gear like poles or axes

You might not be concerned with all of these extras, because it really depends on your trip and your preferences. But if you're spending a lot of time on the trail, it's important to have a pack that fits comfortably and can easily carry all your gear.

How to Pack Your Rucksack for Wild Camping

Packing your rucksack correctly will also help with comfort and stability while on the trail.

To pack a rucksack efficiently, place heavier items like water and food near your spine and towards the middle of the rucksack for balance.

Layer medium-weight items like clothing around them, and put light, bulky items at the bottom. Use outer pockets for essentials you need quick access to, such as maps and snacks.

Distribute weight evenly and make use of compression straps to minimise movement, ensuring a stable and comfortable hike.

Final Thoughts: What Size Rucksack Do You Need for Wild Camping?

Choosing the right rucksack for wild camping boils down to understanding your needs and the nature of your adventure. Whether you're setting out for a quick overnighter or an extended expedition, the size and features of your rucksack can make or break your experience.

Is a 40L Backpack Big Enough for Camping?

A 40L backpack is typically sufficient for minimalist or weekend camping, accommodating essentials like a small tent, sleeping bag, food, and clothing. However, for longer trips or if you carry additional equipment, a larger capacity or external attachments might be necessary to ensure you have everything you need.

Do You Need More Than One Pack for Wild Camping?

Whether you need more than one pack for wild camping depends on the trip's duration, your gear requirements, and how much you can comfortably carry. For most, a single, well-organised rucksack is sufficient, but additional packs may be needed for longer excursions, specific equipment, or day hikes.

What is the Difference Between a Rucksack and a Backpack?

The primary difference lies in size and purpose. A rucksack is a larger, rugged bag designed for outdoor activities and extended trips, equipped with various features for carrying heavy loads. A backpack is smaller, used for daily activities or shorter trips, focusing on convenience and light travel.

title: 10 Stress-Free Lunch Ideas When Camping With the Kids
author: Laurence
excerpt: If you’re looking for some quick, easy, and stress-free lunch ideas when camping with the kids, we’ve got some super recommendations that you can whip up in not time at all. Making sure you’re well prepared on your trip
html:
If you’re looking for some quick, easy, and stress-free lunch ideas when camping with the kids, we’ve got some super recommendations that you can whip up in not time at all.

Making sure you’re well prepared on your trip with meal ideas is essential, especially when you’re camping with little ones who can be picky eaters. These lunch ideas are not only kid-approved, but they’re also convenient and won’t require a lot of time or effort to make.

So whether you’re off on a 10-day campsite trip or a long weekend away, these lunch ideas will keep everyone’s bellies full and happy.

10 Easy Camping Food Ideas to Make the Kids Happy:

  1. Pasta salads
  2. Vegetable & hummus platter
  3. Pre-made wraps
  4. Foil packet meals
  5. Tomato soup with grilled cheese sandwiches
  6. Baked potatoes
  7. Skewers
  8. Vacuum-sealed packs
  9. Chilli
  10. Burgers & hotdogs

#1 Pasta Salads

Pasta salads are a great option; they can be made in advance and easily stored in a cooler bag to take on your camping adventures. Plus, they are versatile and can be made to suit everyone's tastes. 

Try adding some grilled chicken or veggies for an extra boost of protein and nutrients.

Our Summit To Eat Salmon and Broccoli Pasta is the perfect choice for a quick, easy, and delicious pasta salad. Plus, it’s lightweight and easy to pack, so these packets won’t take up much room in your food storage or cooler bag.

Shop All Summit To Eat Meals

#2 Vegetable & Hummus Platter

Another quick and easy lunch option is a colourful vegetable and hummus platter; kids love dipping, and this encourages them to eat their veggies!

Just pack a variety of chopped vegetables and some hummus for dipping (shop-bought if you don’t have time to make your own). This option requires no cooking and is perfect for hot days.

#3 Pre-Made Wraps

Wraps are another great option for a quick and easy lunch while camping with the kids. You can make them ahead of time and then store them in a cooler bag ready for the next day. 

Some ideas could include turkey and avocado, ham and cheese, or veggie and hummus. For added nutrition and fibre, opt for wholegrain wraps as opposed to white wraps.

You can also get creative with fillings and let the kids choose their own combinations. This adds an element of fun to mealtime and encourages them to try new foods.

#4 Foil Packet Meals

For a twist, try 'foil packet meals'. Simply combine slices of sausage, potatoes, carrots, and onions in aluminium foil and cook them over the campfire for a smoky, delicious meal without any pans to wash.

These meals are easy to prep ahead of time and can be customised with your favourite vegetables and proteins.

#5 Tomato Soup with Cheese Toasties

Another easy camping favourite is tomato soup with cheese toasties, which can be cooked on a camp stove or over the fire, providing a comforting and satisfying meal. 

For the grilled cheese sandwiches, pack sliced bread and your choice of cheese, and the soup can be bought ahead of time to make the cooking process even easier.

#6 Baked Potatoes

Baked potatoes are a classic camping meal that can be easily upgraded with various toppings.

Simply wrap your potatoes in foil and place them over the campfire, turning occasionally until they are soft and cooked through. 

Then, top with your favourite toppings, like baked beans and cheese, for a hearty and filling lunch option.

You can even opt for our Firepot Posh Baked Beans, which come in a convenient pouch and are ready to eat in just a few minutes.

#7 Skewers

Skewers are a fun way to get the kids involved when making lunch while camping, and they also require minimal cleanup.

To make the perfect skewer, start by threading your chosen ingredients onto a long skewer stick. Then, cook over the campfire until they are cooked through and slightly charred. 

The best part is that everyone can customise their own skewer with their favourite ingredients.

#8 Vacuum-Sealed Packs

Vacuum-sealed packs of food are a great option for longer camping trips, as they can be easily stored and transported without taking up too much space.

These packs come in a variety of options, such as pre-cooked meals or raw ingredients like meat and vegetables. 

Simply heat them up over the campfire or on a portable stove for a quick and convenient meal.

#9 Chilli

Chilli can easily be made ahead of time and stored in a sealed container or freezer bag for easy reheating at the campsite.

It's a hearty and filling meal that is perfect for colder camping nights. Plus, it can be easily customised with your choice of ingredients.

Or, if you don’t want to spend time making the chilli from scratch, the dehydrated FirePot Chilli Con Carne and Rice is a delicious option that only requires boiling water to prepare. You can also serve with rice and tortilla chips and have a Mexican cuisine night!

#10 Burgers & Hotdogs

A classic camping meal that never fails to disappoint. These can be easily prepared and cooked over the campfire or on a portable grill.

For a healthier option, consider using turkey or veggie burgers instead of traditional beef patties.

Don't forget the buns and sides like chips or potato salad!

Summary: Easy Camping Meals for Your Next Trip

With these 10 tasty camping food ideas, you'll be sure to keep your little campers happy and well-fed during your next camping trip. 

Whether you prefer sandwiches, wraps, or grilling up some burgers and hotdogs over the fire, there's something for everyone in this list.

Check out our range of camping meals to save even more time and effort during your outdoor adventures.

Shop the Best Food for Camping

FAQs

What If Someone Has Dietary Restrictions or Allergies?

Most of these lunch ideas can be tailored to suit specific dietary restrictions. For example, opt for gluten-free bread instead of traditional bread for sandwiches. 

Just be sure to pack the necessary alternative ingredients.

What Food Can I Take Camping Without a Fridge?

You should opt for non-perishable foods, such as canned meats, dried fruits and dry pasta. 

These types of food can be safely stored without refrigeration, and you also don’t need to worry about them spoiling.

What Is An Easy Camping Breakfast for Kids?

Some easy breakfast options include overnight oats, campfire french toast, or even just cereal when you need something quick and easy.

You could even pack some fresh fruit and yoghurts, but make sure to keep these in a cooler box with ice packs to keep them fresh.

title: How Do You Get Electricity When Camping? A Beginner's Camp Guide
author: Laurence
excerpt: Having a reliable supply of electricity when camping is super important if you’re going to rely on it to power your electronics, lighting, and cooking appliances. But what is the best way to get your leccy when you're ou
html:
Having a reliable supply of electricity when camping is super important if you’re going to rely on it to power your electronics, lighting, and cooking appliances. But what is the best way to get your leccy when you're out in the great outdoors? 

Well, there are a few ways – from simple portable chargers to big generators –  depending on what your camping setup looks like and how much power you need.

We’re going to take you through the different options available, as well as some tips on how to make the most of your electricity while camping.

In this Guide...

  • Knowing Your Electricity Needs While Camping 
    • Assess Your Camping Devices & Appliances   
    • Consider the Duration of Your Camping Trip  
  • The Best Options for Accessing Electricity When Camping
    • #1 Portable Power Stations  
    • #2 Solar Panels  
    • #3 Battery Banks  
    • #4 Generators  
  • Practical Tips for Managing Electricity Usage on Your Trip
    • #1 Consider Energy Conservation Strategies  
    • #2 Plan & Prepare for Your Camping Electricity Needs  
    • #3 Carry Out Safety & Maintenance Checks
  • Summary: The Best Electricity Sources When Camping
  • FAQs

    Knowing Your Electricity Needs While Camping 

    Before deciding on the best way to access electricity during your camping trip, it's crucial to assess your specific needs. This will help you determine the most suitable and efficient solution. 

    Assess Your Camping Devices & Appliances   

    Camping electricity requirements can vary widely depending on the devices and appliances you plan to use. 

    Start by making a list of all the items you'll need to power, such as lanterns, torches, portable fans, phones, tablets, cameras, and even small camping stoves or coffee makers. 

    Estimate the power consumption of each device and calculate the total energy requirements. 

    Consider the Duration of Your Camping Trip  

    The length of your camping trip is another key factor to consider. 

    A short weekend getaway may only require a minimal amount of electricity, whereas an extended stay could necessitate more substantial power solutions. 

    The Best Options for Accessing Electricity When Camping

    As for the options for accessing electricity, there are a few different routes you can take.

    You might even want to consider opting for more than one of these sources to ensure you have enough power for your entire trip, or to power your different devices and appliances separately.

    #1 Portable Power Stations  

    Portable power stations are essentially large battery packs designed to provide electricity on the go. 

    These devices can store a significant amount of energy and typically feature multiple outlets and USB ports for charging various devices. 

    They're compact and relatively lightweight, and they can be recharged using solar panels or wall outlets before your trip. 

    However, they can be expensive, and their battery capacity may be limited for extended trips or high-energy needs. 

    #2 Solar Panels  

    Harnessing the power of the sun is an environmentally friendly and renewable way to access electricity while camping. 

    Solar panels come in various sizes and styles, from compact foldable models to larger rigid panels. 

    The efficiency of solar panels can vary, with more expensive options typically performing better in low-light conditions. 

    To optimise solar panel performance, position them in direct sunlight and adjust their angle throughout the day. 

    Keep in mind that cloudy weather or shaded areas can significantly reduce their output.

    #3 Battery Banks  

    For powering smaller devices like phones, tablets, or cameras, high-capacity battery banks can be a convenient solution. 

    These portable chargers are lightweight and easy to carry, making them ideal for shorter camping trips or as a backup power source. 

    When selecting a battery bank, consider the total capacity (measured in milliamp-hours or mAh) and the number of available ports for simultaneous charging.

    #4 Generators  

    Petrol or propane-powered generators offer a more robust and reliable source of electricity for camping, particularly for powering larger appliances or running multiple devices simultaneously. 

    However, they can be noisy, require fuel, and produce emissions, which may not be ideal in pristine natural environments. 

    Practical Tips for Managing Electricity Usage on Your Trip

    When it comes to managing electricity on a camping trip, there are a few key factors you should consider to ensure that you have enough electricity to last you through your trip while also being mindful of the environment and those around you.

    #1 Consider Energy Conservation Strategies  

    Conserving energy is not only environmentally friendly but can also extend the life of your power sources. 

    Simple habits like turning off devices when not in use, dimming or reducing the number of lights, and unplugging chargers from power sources when not charging can go a long way in minimising energy waste. 

    Additionally, prioritise your electricity needs and focus on powering essential devices first, such as lighting or communication devices. 

    #2 Plan & Prepare for Your Camping Electricity Needs  

    Proper planning and preparation are key to ensuring a smooth and stress-free camping experience when it comes to electricity usage. 

    Before your trip, create a checklist of camping gear you'll need, including power sources, cables, adapters, and any necessary backup equipment. 

    Charge all your devices and power sources fully before departure, and consider bringing spare batteries or an extra portable charger. 

    It's also a good idea to test your equipment beforehand to ensure everything is working correctly. 

    #3 Carry Out Safety & Maintenance Checks

    Handling electrical devices in an outdoor setting requires extra precautions. 

    Keep your equipment dry and protected from the elements, and avoid using devices or charging cables in wet conditions. 

    If you're camping in a high-risk area for lightning storms, take appropriate safety measures and unplug devices during storms. 

    Regular maintenance of your power sources, such as cleaning solar panels or checking generator oil levels, can help ensure optimal performance and longevity. 

    Follow the manufacturer's recommendations for proper care and storage of your equipment. 

    Summary: The Best Electricity Sources When Camping

    There are plenty of ways you can get your electricity when camping, from traditional generators to solar panels. However, it's important to handle these devices with care and take proper precautions to ensure safe and reliable use in an outdoor environment.

    For more camping tips and advice, we recommend heading over to our full blog, where you’ll find guides on planning and prepping for a smooth, safe, and enjoyable camping trip.

    Click Here to Read More of our Blog

    FAQs

    Can I Use a Regular Extension Cord to Power Devices From My Car's Battery?

    It's not recommended that you use regular extension cords as they can drain your car's battery quickly. 

    Instead, invest in a dedicated power inverter designed for automotive use, which will safely and efficiently convert your battery's DC power to AC power for devices.

    How Do I Calculate the Power Requirements For My Camping Gear?

    Check the wattage or amperage rating on each device and add them up. 

    As a general rule, multiply watts by hours of usage to estimate the battery capacity needed in watt-hours (Wh) or amp-hours (Ah).

    Are Gas-Powered Generators Allowed In All Campsites?

    No, many campgrounds restrict or prohibit the use of noisy generators, especially in quiet hours. 

    Always check the campground rules beforehand and prioritise clean, quiet power sources like solar or battery packs when possible.

    How Can I Maximise Solar Panel Efficiency While Camping?

    Position panels in direct sunlight, angling them perpendicularly to the sun's rays. Use a sun tracker or reposition panels periodically.

    Keep panels clean, unobstructed by trees/buildings, and avoid shaded areas which reduce output significantly.

title: How to Build a Campfire in 5 Easy Steps
author: Laurence
excerpt: Knowing how to build a campfire is a must-have skill for any camper or outdoor enthusiast – and it’s a lot easier than you may think. Not only is a good from a practical point, but a crackling fire can also create a cosy
html:
Knowing how to build a campfire is a must-have skill for any camper or outdoor enthusiast – and it’s a lot easier than you may think.

Not only is a good from a practical point, but a crackling fire can also create a cosy ambience and provide warmth on chilly nights (not to mention be brilliant for toasting marshmallows!).

But before you start gathering wood and striking matches, there are a few important things to consider. Follow these 5 easy steps to build the perfect campfire and enjoy a memorable night under the stars.

Preparing to Build Your Campfire

Before you begin building your campfire, it’s essential to carry out the necessary preparations beforehand to make sure it's done both safely and efficiently. 

The two main things you'll need to consider are the location and the materials needed…

Selecting the Right Location 

Choosing the right location for your campfire is essential for maintaining safety and adhering to local regulations. 

Look for a clear, level area away from tents, overhanging branches, and any flammable materials. It's recommended to maintain at least a 15-foot clearance from tents, trees, and other combustible objects. 

Additionally, check with local authorities regarding any specific regulations or restrictions on campfires in the area you'll be visiting.  

Gathering Materials 

To build a successful campfire, you'll need three types of materials: tinder, kindling, and fuel wood. 

How to Build a Campfire in 5 Steps

With the necessary preparations complete, it's time to start building your campfire. Follow these step-by-step instructions to construct a safe and long-lasting fire. 

Step 1: Clearing the Ground  

Begin by clearing the area where you plan to build the fire. Remove any dry leaves, twigs, or other debris that could potentially catch fire and spread uncontrollably. 

Step 2: Creating a Fire Pit  

If permitted in the area, you can create a fire pit by digging a shallow depression in the ground. This will help contain the fire and prevent it from spreading. 

Step 3: Arranging Your Tinder  

In the centre of the cleared area or fire pit, create a small mound or nest with your tinder materials. This will be the base for igniting your fire. 

Step 4: Choosing a Fire Layout  

There are several ways to arrange the kindling and fuel wood around your tinder nest. 

Fire Arrangement What It Is
Teepee Arranging the kindling and fuel wood in a cone-like shape over the tinder.
Log Cabin Stacking the kindling and fuel wood in a square or rectangular shape, resembling a miniature log cabin.
Lean-To Leaning the kindling and fuel wood against a larger log or rock, creating a tent-like structure.

Step 5: Arranging the Kindling & Fuel Wood  

Whichever layout you choose, start by placing the kindling over the tinder nest, leaving enough space for air to circulate. 

Then, add larger pieces of fuel wood around or on top of the kindling, creating a sturdy structure.

How to Maintain & Manage Your Campfire

Sustaining the fire for the desired duration is key. Monitor the fuel levels and add more wood as needed to keep the fire going. 

However, be careful not to overload the fire, as this can cause it to become uncontrollable. 

Aim for a steady, consistent burn by adding a few pieces of fuel wood at a time. 

Techniques for adjusting the fire's size and heat output are also valuable skills to have. If the fire is burning too hot or too large, you can control it by spreading the burning logs apart or using a shovel to scoop some of the burning material out of the fire pit. 

Conversely, if the fire is burning too low, you can bring the burning logs closer together or add more kindling or small pieces of fuel wood to increase the heat output. 

Here are some tips on adding fuel and stoking the fire:

  • Use a long stick or fire poker to stoke the fire and reposition the burning logs gently.
  • Add larger pieces of fuel wood to the edge of the fire pit, allowing them to catch fire before pushing them into the centre.
  • Avoid adding too much fuel at once, as this can smother the fire and produce excessive smoke.
  • Rotate the fuel wood periodically to ensure even burning.

How to Safely & Properly Extinguish the Campfire

Knowing how to build a campfire isn’t the only important skill to have when camping. It’s also crucial to know how to properly extinguish the fire before leaving the campsite.

Follow these steps to safely extinguish your campfire:

Step 1: Stop Adding Fuel  

Once you've determined it's time to extinguish the fire, stop adding any additional fuel, wood or kindling. Allow the existing materials to burn down to a manageable level. 

Step 2: Douse with Water  

Using a bucket or other container filled with water, slowly pour water onto the burning logs and embers. 

Be careful not to smother the fire too quickly, as this can cause a sudden burst of smoke and ash. 

Step 3: Stir the Ashes  

After dousing the fire with water, use a stick to spread the ashes. This will help expose any remaining hot spots or embers that may still be burning. 

Step 4: Repeat as Needed  

Continue to pour water and stir the ashes until you're certain the fire is completely extinguished. Touch the ashes with your hands to ensure they're cool to the touch.

Summary: Simple Steps to Building a Campfire 

Building a campfire is a rewarding and memorable experience that can enhance any outdoor adventure, and by following the steps outlined in this guide, you'll be equipped with the knowledge and skills necessary to safely and efficiently construct your own campfire. 

At JustSupplies, we’ve got a wide range of tools and accessories to help making fire at your campsite a breeze. From fuel blocks and tinder sticks to matches and fire starters, you’ll find everything you need to get your fire going in no time.

Shop Fire-Making Equipment

FAQs

Can I Use Green Or Wet Wood For a Campfire?

No, green or wet wood should be avoided as it will produce excessive smoke and struggle to burn properly. 

Always use dry, seasoned wood that has been appropriately cured to ensure an efficient and clean burning fire.

How Can I Keep My Campfire Burning For An Extended Period? 

To sustain your campfire, continually add fuel wood in moderation, being careful not to smother the flames. 

Rotate and reposition the burning logs periodically, and use a stick or poker to gently stoke the fire and increase airflow.

How Do I Know If My Campfire Is Completely Extinguished?

Douse the fire thoroughly with water and stir the ashes, exposing any remaining hot spots. 

Repeat this process until the ashes are cool to the touch. Once cooled, disperse the ashes and restore the area before leaving.

html:
Whether you're looking to unwind in the serene Highlands or enjoy the coastal vistas of the Isle of Skye, Scotland offers an unparalleled variety of camping experiences.

The country's rich tapestry of lush landscapes, towering mountains, and tranquil lochs make it a favourable destination for both seasoned campers and those new to the outdoor experience. 

Our comprehensive overview will ensure you find the ideal spot to set up your tent and enjoy everything Scotland has to offer.

Legal Guidelines for Camping

Before setting out on your camping trip in Scotland, it's crucial to be familiar with the Scottish Outdoor Access Code, which provides detailed guidance on responsible camping.

The code allows you to camp on most unenclosed land, but it's important to follow specific rules, especially when wild camping.

You must avoid enclosed fields and always camp at a reasonable distance from residential properties and roads.

Campers should minimise their impact on the environment by taking all rubbish home and avoiding open fires.

By respecting these guidelines, you ensure that the pristine nature of Scotland remains unspoilt for fellow adventurers and future generations.

Understanding and adhering to these regulations will make your camping experience both enjoyable and respectful towards the environment and local communities.

10 of the Best Camping Sites in Scotland

Scotland has some of the most breathtaking and diverse landscapes in the country, making it a popular destination for camping enthusiasts. 

Whether you prefer pitching your tent on a remote beach or being nestled in the heart of the mountains, there is something for every type of camper in Scotland.

But with so many options to choose from, where should you start?

Top 5 Scottish Campsites for Amenities & Comfort

Scotland offers a variety of campsites that combine the beauty of the great outdoors with the comfort and amenities that make camping a relaxing and enjoyable experience. 

Here are five top campsites renowned for their facilities and stunning locations:

1) Horgabost Campsite on the Isle of Harris

Located in the village of Horgabost on the West Coast of Harris, Horgabost Campsite offers stunning views of white sandy beaches and crystal-clear waters. 

The facilities on offer include hot showers, a wash-up area, and a fridge for communal use. 

2) Invercaimbe Caravan & Camping, Arisaig

This family-run campsite offers a range of facilities, including electric hook-up points, a laundry and dishwashing room, and showers. 

You will also be a short distance from the stunning beaches of Arisaig, where you can enjoy a day full of swimming, sunbathing, and exploring.

3) Port Mor Campsite, Isle of Islay

Port Mor Campsite is located near Port Charlotte, known for its beautiful beaches and whiskey distilleries. The campsite itself has a café and free internet access, as well as access to fresh water.

4) Ardnamurchan Campsite, Lochaber

Staying at Ardnamurchan Campsite will put you in close proximity to the volcanic land and picturesque beaches of West Ardnamurchan. 

Facilities include electric hook-up points and direct access to the beach.

5) Sands Caravan and Camping Park, Gairloch

This campsite has a grocery shop, toilet and shower blocks, and a games and TV room. 

It is surrounded by the stunning scenery of Gairloch, with nearby hikes and water activities available.

Top 5 Locations for Wild Camping

Scotland is renowned for its wild camping opportunities, allowing campers to connect directly with nature. 

Unlike the rest of the UK, you can wild camp just about anywhere in the home of the Scots, with vast swathes of unspoilt landscapes waiting for you.

But with so many incredible locations to choose from, where should you pitch your tent? Here are our top 5 picks for wild camping destinations in Scotland.

1) Bonaly Reservoir, near Edinburgh

Located just a short drive from Edinburgh city centre, Bonaly Reservoir is the perfect spot for wild camping. It offers stunning views of the Pentland Hills and easy access to hiking trails.

2) Barrisdale, Knoydart

Knoydart is a secluded and remote location with breathtaking views of Loch Hourn. The rugged terrain and lack of amenities make it a true wild camping experience.

3) Glenfeshie, Cairngorms National Park

Known for its huge array of wildlife, Glenfeshie is a popular spot for wild camping. It also offers stunning views of the surrounding mountains and forests.

17 Must-Have Wild Camping Essentials

4) Rackwick Bay, Orkney

Rackwick Bay is a remote and peaceful spot for wild camping. It offers spectacular views of the North Sea and the coastal town of Rackwick has a small number of tourist amenities on offer.

5) Gleann na Muice, Fisherfield

Gleann na Muice is the perfect camping spot for those who enjoy mountain climbing. Located in the Fisherfield Forest, it offers access to some of Scotland's most challenging peaks.

Essential Gear for Scottish Camping

Preparing adequately with the right gear is crucial for a successful camping trip in Scotland. The weather can be a little unpredictable, so you’ll want to make sure you’re covered for all eventualities.

Use this as a bit of a checklist before heading out on your Scottish camping adventure:

  • A sturdy, waterproof tent is essential, as weather conditions can change rapidly. Choose a tent with a robust flysheet and a high hydrostatic head rating to withstand heavy rain and gusty winds.
  • A sleeping bag rated for three or four seasons will ensure warmth during cooler nights, especially in the Highlands.
  • A portable stove, as relying on campfires is often not viable due to environmental regulations and the wet Scottish climate. Include waterproof matches or a wind-resistant lighter.
  • Clothing should be layered, breathable, and waterproof, with a reliable set of boots for hiking across varied terrains.
  • Navigation tools such as a map and compass are indispensable, given the remote nature of many Scottish camping spots.
  • Finally, a first-aid kit, insect repellent (especially for midge season), and a headlamp or torch round out the essential gear list.

Conclusion

Exploring Scotland through camping, whether at well-equipped campsites or in the wild expanses of its rugged terrain, offers an incomparable connection to nature. 

With the right preparation, respect for legal guidelines, and commitment to sustainability, you can fully enjoy the serene beauty and rich biodiversity of Scotland. 

Remember to pack appropriately, respect the wildlife and environment, and choose your camping spots wisely. 

By doing so, you ensure that these magnificent landscapes remain pristine and accessible for future adventurers. Happy camping!

FAQs

Can You Wild Camp in Scottish National Parks?

Yes, wild camping is allowed in most Scottish national parks as long as you follow the Scottish Outdoor Access Code. However, some areas may have restrictions or require a permit, so it's important to check beforehand.

Can You Camp in Laybys in Scotland?

For the most part, camping in laybys is not allowed in Scotland. There are, however, some exceptions, so it’s best to check local restrictions.

Where Can You Wild Camp in England & Wales?

Wild camping is generally not allowed in England and Wales unless you have permission from the landowner. However, there are some areas that allow wild camping with certain restrictions.

title: 10 Boredom-Busting Games to Play When Camping With Your Pals
author: Laurence
excerpt: If you’ve been assigned the job of planner for your friends camping trip, you may be feeling the pressure to come up with fun activities to do while on your getaway. Well, we’ve got a list of great games to play when cam
html:
If you’ve been assigned the job of planner for your friends camping trip, you may be feeling the pressure to come up with fun activities to do while on your getaway. Well, we’ve got a list of great games to play when camping that’ll keep everyone entertained.

Whether you're gathered around a roaring campfire, whiling away a rainy day inside your tent, or exploring the woods, these games ensure that every moment is filled with fun and laughter. 

From classic favourites to imaginative new twists, there’s something here to suit every taste and group size.

10 Fun Camping Games to Play With Your Friends:

  1. Truth or dare
  2. Charades
  3. Tent pitching relay
  4. The human knot
  5. Treasure hunt
  6. Flashlight tag
  7. Stargazing bingo
  8. Nature scavenger hunt
  9. Eco-art challenge
  10. Card games

#1 Truth or Dare

'Truth or Dare' remains a staple, providing laughs and deepening friendships as secrets and silliness unfold. 

You could make it lighthearted or ramp up the stakes by including prompts that involve campsite challenges, such as singing a song in front of neighbouring campers.

For the best experience, make sure to have a mix of easy and challenging questions and tasks. 

This game is perfect for small or large groups and can be played by all ages.

#2 Charades

Games like 'Charades' tap into everyone's creative side, as players mime different book titles, movies, or songs for others to guess. 

You can even split into teams and make it a competition! 

This is another great game for all ages but may require some pre-planning to come up with categories or prompts.

#3 Tent Pitching Relay

One popular game that encourages collaboration is 'Tent Pitching Relay', where teams compete to set up and take down a tent the fastest. 

This not only adds an element of fun but also teaches valuable camping skills. 

To make it even more challenging, you can have each team use a different type of tent or give them specific instructions for setting it up.

It's a great way to get everyone involved and working together.

Some of our favourite easy-to-pitch tents include…

#4 The Human Knot

Another engaging team game is 'The Human Knot', where players stand in a circle, grab other people's hands at random, and work together to untangle themselves without letting go.

To add a competitive element, you can time each team and see who can untangle the fastest.

You can also have teams compete to create the most creative human knot sculpture once they are untangled.

#5 Treasure Hunt

For a game that requires a bit of problem-solving, a treasure hunt, where teams use a series of cleverly crafted clues to find hidden items around the campsite, is a great option. 

You can also incorporate specific tasks or challenges that teams must complete at each location to earn extra points.

It's a fantastic way to encourage teamwork, critical thinking, and outdoor exploration.

Just make sure to have a prize for the winning team to add an extra element of competition.

#6 Flashlight Tag

'Flashlight Tag' is a thrilling game where one person, armed with a camping flashlight, seeks out hidden players in the dark, shining a light on them to mark them out.  

The game can be played in various ways, such as using different colours of light to represent different teams or having a time limit for each round.

This game is an exciting way to enjoy the outdoors at night!

Shop now

#7 Stargazing Bingo

For those who enjoy quieter activities, 'Stargazing Bingo' can be a hit; players have cards with different astronomical objects and must spot them in the sky to win. 

This activity encourages quiet observation and helps players learn more about constellations, stars, and planets.

It's a great way to spend an evening outdoors and can even spark interest in astronomy.

#8 Nature Scavenger Hunt

One engaging game is 'Nature Scavenger Hunt', in which players have lists of natural items to find within a set time limit. 

This can include specific types of leaves, stones, or wildlife sightings.

Nature scavenger hunts can even be tailored to different age groups and locations, making the game suitable for all types of outdoor events.

Encourage players to take photos as they find each item and award points for creativity.

#9 Eco-Art Challenge

For a creative twist, try 'Eco-Art Challenge', where groups use found natural materials to create temporary art installations at the campsite. 

This not only encourages creativity but also promotes a deeper connection with the environment. 

To make it more competitive, have judges or fellow campers vote for their favourite installations.

#10 Card Games

For a more traditional approach, 'Card Games' like Rummy, Go Fish, or even Poker can keep everyone entertained for hours. 

They can also be adapted to fit different group sizes and are perfect for playing inside the tent so that when rain strikes, your camping spirit doesn’t need to be dampened.

Bring a deck of cards along for your outdoor adventure and enjoy some friendly competition.

Summary: Fun Camping Activities for Your Next Trip

There is a huge variety of games to play when camping to keep your trip entertaining for all and to make lasting memories. 

From classic campfire games, such as Truth or Dare, to those perfect to play inside your tent during a rainy afternoon, there is something for everyone to get involved in. 

So gather your friends or family around the campfire and get ready for some friendly competition!

FAQs

What Camping Games Can You Play If It Rains?

There are many camping games you can play inside your tent in order to stay out of the rain, such as card and board games.

What Camping Games Can You Play With Kids?

The best camping games for children are those that are easy to play but also engaging. These could include tag and treasure hunts.

What Card Games Can I Play When Camping?

Crazy Eights is a good card game for all ages and you can even have up to 8 players. Other fun card games include Uno, Go Fish, and Old Maid.

Camping on the beach sounds like a seriously relaxing and peaceful way to spend a summer holiday – but can you actually pitch up and camp on the beach in the UK?

Well, it’s really dependent on the beach. There are different rules for different beaches; some have specific camping spots or times of year when it is allowed, whereas others might not allow camping at all.

This article will guide you through the dos and don’ts of beach camping across the UK, ensuring you know exactly what’s allowed and what could land you in hot water.

In this Article:

  • What are the Beach Camping Regulations in the UK?

    What are the Beach Camping Regulations in the UK?

    Beach camping in the UK operates under a complex set of rules that vary significantly by location. 

    Unlike some countries where beach camping is widely permitted, the UK has stringent regulations to protect its coastal environments. 

    In general, camping on beaches without explicit permission from the landowner is not allowed. This includes most publicly owned beaches. 

    However, some beaches do offer designated camping spots or have specific times of the year when camping is tolerated.

    It's crucial to check local council websites or contact local tourist information centres for guidance. This ensures you remain on the right side of the law while enjoying the unique experience of beach camping.

    Regional Variations in Beach Camping Rules

    The rules governing beach camping are not uniform across the UK…

    England & Wales Scotland
    England and Wales typically have stricter controls, with many coastal areas completely off-limits for campers unless specific permission has been granted.  Scotland is generally more lenient due to the Right to Roam Act under the Land Reform (Scotland) Act 2003, which allows responsible wild camping on most unenclosed land. However, certain popular beaches may have restrictions to prevent overcrowding and environmental damage.

    Understanding these regional nuances is vital for planning your beach camping trip, as it helps avoid potential fines and ensures that you respect the natural landscapes you come to enjoy.

    How to Find Beach Camping Locations

    Start by checking the official websites of national parks and nature reserves; some of these areas have designated beach camping spots. 

    Local tourist information centres are also valuable resources. They can provide up-to-date information on where beach camping is permitted and any restrictions you might need to be aware of. 

    Engaging with online camping forums and social media groups can also yield personal recommendations and tips on hidden gems. 

    Our Top Tips for Camping on the Beach

    If you do manage to secure a spot on the beach, you’ll want to make the most of your experience.

    As with any camping trip – regardless of whether it’s on the beach or in the mountains – preparation is key.

    Here are some top tips to keep in mind:

    #1 Beach Camping Safety Tips

    Safety should always be a top priority when camping, particularly at the beach. 

    High tides can alter the shape of the beach dramatically, so make sure to set up your camp above the high tide line. 

    Be aware of local wildlife; some areas may have jellyfish, sharp shells, or even biting insects. 

    Bring a first-aid kit equipped for minor injuries and possible allergic reactions. 

    Lastly, always inform someone of your camping plans and expected return, just in case you need assistance.

    Shop now

    #2 Beach Camping Etiquette

    Maintaining good etiquette is essential while beach camping to ensure that everyone can enjoy their experience without conflict.

    Keep your campsite tidy and compact to leave as much space as possible for others. 

    Noise can carry far on open beaches, so keep the volume of voices and music down, especially in the evenings. 

    Always follow the beach's rules about fires and make sure to extinguish your camp fire completely to prevent any risks. 

    Respecting other campers and the natural environment helps foster communal respect that makes beach camping enjoyable for everyone.

    Respecting Wildlife & Natural Habitats

    When camping on beaches, it's crucial to respect the surrounding wildlife and their habitats. 

    Coastal areas are often breeding grounds for birds and nesting sites for marine life. Disturbing these environments can have long-lasting negative effects. 

    To minimise your impact, avoid areas marked for wildlife protection and adhere to any local signage about restricted activities. 

    Keep noise levels down, especially at night, and ensure that any lights used are not disrupting wildlife. 

    By being mindful of these practices, campers can coexist peacefully with nature, contributing to the preservation of these vital ecosystems.

    #3 Check the Weather!

    Before heading out on your beach camping trip, be sure to check the weather forecast for the duration of your stay. 

    This will help you prepare and pack accordingly, as well as make any necessary adjustments to your plans.

    In case of inclement weather, it's important to have a backup plan or an alternate location in mind. 

    It's also helpful to pack extra tarps or rain gear just in case.

    You should monitor the weather during your trip and take proper precautions if severe weather is expected.

    #4 Make Sure You Have the Appropriate Camping Gear for the Beach

    When preparing for a beach camping adventure, selecting the right gear is crucial to ensuring comfort and safety. 

    Due to the sandy and often damp environment, a robust tent with a strong groundsheet is essential. 

    A sleeping bag rated for the season and an insulated mat can also make a significant difference in your comfort levels overnight. 

    Additionally, consider a windbreak to shelter your campsite from gusty sea breezes and don't forget a reliable headlamp or lantern for those darker evenings.

    Finally, pack a sturdy rubbish bag to keep the site clean, as beaches often lack facilities. 

    These essentials will help create a more enjoyable and responsible beach camping experience.

    Shop now

    Conclusion: Beach Camping in the UK

    Beach camping in the UK offers a unique opportunity to embrace the stunning natural landscapes that define the coastline, providing a memorable way to connect with nature. 

    It's an adventure that calls for responsibility and respect towards the environment, local wildlife, and fellow campers. 

    By adhering to the regulations, securing the necessary permissions, and practising considerate camping habits, you ensure that these beautiful places remain pristine and accessible for future visitors.

title: How High is Mount Everest Base Camp? Distance, Altitude & Difficulty
author: Laurence
excerpt: Planning a trip to Mount Everest Base Camp? It’s no easy feat, but the rewards of reaching this iconic location are unforgettable. Knowing the important facts like how high Mount Everest Base Camp is, and how difficult i
html:
Planning a trip to Mount Everest Base Camp? It’s no easy feat, but the rewards of reaching this iconic location are unforgettable. Knowing the important facts like how high Mount Everest Base Camp is, and how difficult it can be to reach, is essential for anyone looking to embark on this journey.

To help with your trip prep (or satisfy your curiosity), we’re breaking down everything you need to know about the height, distance, and difficulty of Mount Everest Base Camp. 

From the physical demands to the breathtaking vistas, understanding these elements is crucial for anyone preparing to tread the paths of Everest.

So lace up your boots and let’s get started!

Key points:

  • Everest Base Camp sits 5,364 metres above sea level.
  • The route journeys through the Khumbu region of Nepal.
  • Ensure you are prepared physically, have the right hiking gear, and have all necessary logistics in place before your trip.
  • The ‘climb high, sleep low’ acclimatisation strategy can be used to help your body adjust to decreased oxygen levels.
  • Make sure to travel with a credible trekking company and carry a first-aid kit.
Shop now

What is the Altitude of Mount Everest Base Camp?

This elevation brings with it not only spectacular panoramic views but also significant challenges due to the thin air and lower oxygen levels.

At such heights, trekkers are exposed to the risks associated with acute mountain sickness (AMS), which can affect even the most experienced of climbers.

Understanding the altitude of Everest Base Camp is vital for preparation and acclimatisation planning. 

The reduced oxygen concentration at this elevation demands that trekkers condition their bodies, often several months in advance, to cope with less oxygen.

The Journey to Everest Base Camp

The journey to Everest Base Camp is a trek that captures the essence of adventure through the heart of some of the most breathtaking landscapes on the planet. 

Typically starting from Lukla, the trek spans approximately 130 kilometres round trip and takes about 12 days to complete, including necessary acclimatisation stops.

The route meanders through the rugged Khumbu region of Nepal, offering trekkers a chance to immerse themselves in the natural beauty of towering peaks and vibrant Sherpa culture. 

The distance to the Base Camp is not merely a physical challenge; it is a passage through dramatically changing ecosystems and altitudes that require both physical and mental preparation.

Local Insights & Cultural Aspects

The trek to Everest Base Camp is also a journey through the heart of Sherpa culture. 

The Sherpas, renowned for their mountaineering expertise and deep connection to the Himalayas, play a pivotal role in the Everest expeditions. 

As trekkers wind their way through villages like Phakding, Namche Bazaar, and Tengboche, they encounter rich traditions and a vibrant lifestyle adapted to the harsh mountain environment. 

Visiting local monasteries, participating in cultural ceremonies, and interacting with the welcoming communities provides a profound insight into the lives of the people who call this region home. 

Furthermore, the journey offers a glimpse into sustainable tourism practices that benefit the local economy and preserve the natural environment. 

Embracing these cultural experiences adds a significant layer of depth to the trek, turning an adventurous expedition into a meaningful encounter with Nepalese heritage and hospitality.

The Challenges of Trekking to Mount Everest Base Camp

Trekking to Everest Base Camp is not without its array of physical and environmental hurdles. 

The physical demands of the trek involve long days of walking – often six to eight hours – over uneven and sometimes steep terrain. 

The environmental aspect includes dealing with extreme weather conditions, which can vary dramatically between sunny, clear mornings and sudden snowfall or chilling winds. 

Altitude adds another layer of complexity, with temperatures dropping below freezing as trekkers ascend higher, making proper hiking or trekking gear and physical resilience essential components for success. 

Additionally, the thinning air not only makes breathing laborious but also slows down the recovery process, making each step a testament to the trekker's endurance and willpower.

Shop All Hiking Gear

How to Prepare for the Base Camp Trek: Our Top Tips

Properly preparing for your trek is very important. It won’t be a case of upping and leaving one day for the base camp trek. It takes weeks of preparation and training to get your body physically and mentally ready for this challenging adventure.

Our most important tips include…

#1 Work On Your Physical Fitness 

Prospective trekkers should engage in comprehensive physical training that mimics the conditions of high-altitude hiking; this includes cardiovascular exercises such as running, cycling, and swimming, alongside strength training focused on the legs, back, and core.

The trek will involve strenuous and long days of hiking, so it is crucial to build up endurance and strength before embarking on the journey.

#2 Ensure You Have the Right Gear

Equally important is investing in quality gear specifically designed for cold, windy, and wet conditions. 

Not only that, but you’ll need food, water, and a backpack to carry everything in.

It is essential to pack lightweight, durable items that won’t weigh you down during the trek. This includes packing high-energy snacks and plenty of water to stay hydrated throughout the journey.

A lightweight backpack like the Exped Radical Lite Folding Rucksack is great for this trip. The 50L option is spacious enough to hold all your gear while still being compact and easy to carry, with quick access to your essentials with the centre zip design.

Additionally, consider bringing a pair of trekking poles to help with balance and stability on uneven terrain. These can also provide support for your knees and reduce strain on your joints during long hikes.

#3 Plan Logistics in Advance

Trekkers should plan their journey meticulously, considering travel insurance, necessary vaccinations, and obtaining the appropriate permits. 

This preparation not only enhances safety but also ensures a more enjoyable and immersive experience amidst the challenges of high-altitude trekking.

#4 Acclimatisation Strategies

Acclimatisation is a critical component of any high-altitude trek, particularly one that reaches the heights of Everest Base Camp. 

The process involves gradual exposure to higher altitudes to allow the body to adjust to decreased oxygen levels.

Trekkers are advised to incorporate rest days into their itinerary, particularly in key locations like Namche Bazaar and Dingboche, which are known for assisting with altitude adaptation. 

Hydration and a balanced diet are also vital, as dehydration can exacerbate altitude sickness symptoms. 

Safety Measures & Emergency Preparedness for the Trek

Safety on the journey to Everest Base Camp is paramount, given the remote nature of the route and the extreme conditions faced at high altitudes. 

Every trekker must be prepared for potential emergencies, which include weather changes, altitude sickness, and injuries. 

Key safety measures include travelling with a reputable trekking company that provides experienced guides who are trained in first aid and emergency response. 

It is advisable to carry a well-equipped first aid kit, along with access to communication devices, such as satellite phones or radios, in case of emergency. 

Moreover, ensuring that you have a clear understanding of the nearest medical facilities and evacuation procedures is crucial. 

Many trekkers also opt for travel insurance that covers high-altitude trekking and emergency evacuation, providing an additional layer of security. 

Conclusion: Preparing for Your Everest Base Camp Trip

The trek to Everest Base Camp remains one of the most exhilarating adventures on the planet, offering not only a physical challenge but also a profound personal and cultural experience.

To make sure you’re equipped for your journey, make sure to check out our range of hiking gear, which includes equipment from some of the best brands in the business. From hiking poles to comfortable (and durable) boots, we have everything you need to make your trek a success.

title: Your Guide to the Everest Base Camp: The Cost & Planning Your Trip
author: Laurence
excerpt: Planning your trek to Mount Everest Base Camp involves understanding various critical elements, such as the best season to visit, the detailed routes available and, crucially, how much it costs to go to Everest Base Camp
html:
Planning your trek to Mount Everest Base Camp involves understanding various critical elements, such as the best season to visit, the detailed routes available and, crucially, how much it costs to go to Everest Base Camp. 

We’ve included everything you need to know about the cost of trekking to Everest Base Camp, including the permits you’ll need and the hiking gear you’ll have to bring, as well as the best time to go.

After all, you can never be too prepared when it comes to conquering the world's highest peak!

The important facts:

  • The best times to visit are from March to May and September to November.
  • The classic trekking route starts from Lukla, but the Gokyo Lakes route provides a harder alternative.
  • A standard 12 to 14-day trek costs between £1,200 and £4,000 per person.
  • Make sure to incorporate acclimatisation days into your itinerary.
  • You will need a Sagarmatha National Park permit and a TIMS card.
  • Ensure you have a first-aid kit and an emergency evacuation plan.

What is the Best Time to Visit Everest Base Camp?

Selecting the optimal time to visit Everest Base Camp is paramount to ensuring a successful trek. 

The best periods are typically from March to May and from September to November. 

These months feature the most stable weather conditions, with clearer skies and less precipitation, which not only enhances safety but also improves your chances of unobstructed mountain views. 

During these times, temperatures are generally more comfortable for trekking, although nights can still be quite cold. 

It's also important to consider that these peak seasons can be quite crowded along the trail. 

If you prefer solitude, planning your trek for the edges of these seasons might be beneficial, although you might encounter less predictable weather.

Base Camp Trekking Routes to Choose From

When planning a trek to Everest Base Camp, several routes are available, each offering unique experiences and challenges…

Each itinerary offers its own set of villages, scenic views, and opportunities for cultural immersion, making it crucial to align your choice with your fitness level, trekking experience, and personal interests in the Himalayan landscape.

How Much Does it Cost to Go to Everest Base Camp?

The actual costs of the trek can vary widely depending on your choices regarding guides, porters, travel style, and the trekking agency you choose. 

Typically, a standard 12 to 14-day trek costs between £1,200 and £4,000 per person. 

This budget should cover your round-trip flights from Kathmandu to Lukla, which usually range from £240 to £320. 

Accommodations and meals in teahouses along the trek typically cost between £20 and £24 per day. 

Additionally, permit fees, including the Sagarmatha National Park permit and the TIMS card, total around £32. 

It's also essential to factor in the cost of hiring guides and porters, who are invaluable for their local knowledge and assistance with logistics; guides cost about £28 to £32 per day, while porters cost around £20 per day.

Permits You Will Need for Your Trek

All trekkers are required to obtain a Sagarmatha National Park permit, which helps fund the conservation efforts in the region.

Additionally, a TIMS (Trekkers' Information Management System) card is mandatory for all trekkers in Nepal to ensure their safety and to manage the number of visitors.

These permits can be arranged either in Kathmandu or through your trekking agency.

Ensure that you keep these permits accessible during the trek, as you will need to present them at various checkpoints along the route.

What Essential Gear & Supplies Do You Need for the Trek?

Equipping yourself with the right gear is essential for the harsh conditions of high-altitude trekking. 

Key items include…

  • A sturdy pair of hiking boots
  • A durable backpack, like the Naturehike 500D Waterproof Dry Bag or the Exped Radical Lite Folding Lightweight Rucksack.
  • Suitable trekking poles.

Given the cold temperatures, especially at higher altitudes and during the night, also consider taking with you…

  • Thermal clothing
  • A down jacket
  • A quality sleeping bag rated for sub-zero temperatures, such as the Bushmen Walker 3 Sleeping Bag.

Also, since weather patterns can change rapidly, include waterproof clothing and layering options to adapt easily. 

Other vital supplies include…

  • A first-aid kit
  • Sunscreen
  • Sunglasses for the strong UV rays
  • A headlamp or torch for early morning or late evening treks
  • Hydration solutions like water purification tablets or a portable water filter (staying hydrated is crucial to preventing altitude sickness).
Shop now

Travel Arrangements & Logistics for the Trek

Organising your travel to and from the Everest Base Camp trek involves several key steps. 

Initially, international travellers will need to book flights to Kathmandu, the capital of Nepal, which serves as the starting point for the journey. 

From there, a domestic flight to Lukla – often referred to as the gateway to Everest – is required. 

This flight is famously short and scenic, but due to the high-altitude conditions of the Himalayas, it can also be quite turbulent. 

In Kathmandu, it’s advisable to spend a day or two preparing, purchasing any last-minute supplies, and possibly meeting your guide or trekking group. 

Consider the logistics of travel insurance that covers high-altitude trekking. 

Lastly, arrange your transportation back to Kathmandu post-trek, keeping flexibility in your schedule as flights from Lukla can often be delayed due to weather conditions.

How to Stay Safe When Trekking to Everest B. Camp

Trekking to the Base Camp is physically demanding and poses several health risks, primarily due to the high altitude. 

Preparing for and preventing altitude sickness is paramount; symptoms can include headaches, nausea, and dizziness. 

It is crucial to incorporate acclimatisation days into your itinerary, allowing your body to adjust to the elevation gradually. 

Ensure you are physically prepared for the trek with cardiovascular and strength training months in advance. 

On the trail, maintain hydration and eat regular, energy-rich meals to sustain your energy levels. 

Trekking with a knowledgeable guide who can navigate the route and manage any health issues that arise enhances safety. 

Carrying a basic first aid kit and having a plan for emergency evacuation are essential safety measures.

How to Stay Environmentally Conscious While Trekking

Preserving the pristine environment of the Everest region is a responsibility shared by all who trek it. 

As part of your preparation, learn about the Leave No Trace principles, which include guidelines for minimising waste, respecting wildlife, and preserving the natural environment. 

Use designated campsites and teahouses, dispose of waste properly, and avoid single-use plastics by carrying reusable water bottles and bags. 

Energy use in the region is limited, so be mindful of your consumption. 

Additionally, participating in or donating to local conservation efforts can contribute positively to the long-term sustainability of this iconic destination. 

Conclusion & Final Checklist

As you prepare to conclude your preparations for the Everest Base Camp trek, a final checklist can ensure that nothing is overlooked. 

First, confirm all your travel bookings and double-check that your insurance coverage is appropriate for high-altitude trekking and includes emergency evacuation. 

Review your packing list to verify that you have all the necessary gear, clothing, and medical supplies. 

It’s also wise to have a contingency plan for potential delays or changes in weather conditions.

Finally, mentally prepare for the challenges ahead; maintaining a positive and resilient mindset can be just as crucial as your physical preparations.

With these comprehensive preparations in place, you’re set to tackle one of the most rewarding adventures available to trekkers worldwide.

Planning a summer holiday trip camping with the kids? Rather than let the stress take over, use our guide to make it a fun and memorable experience for the whole family. 

As your kids enter different phases of life and development, it can get harder to keep everyone happy and entertained. 

The eldest isn’t interested in doing anything other than lounging in the tent, while the youngest is constantly getting into mischief, and suddenly you’re dealing with multiple tantrums and boredom-induced meltdowns.

But a little bit of planning goes a long way when it comes to camping with kids. 

We've got some sound tips, tricks, and hacks to help you survive the great outdoors with your little ones.

    Tips to Make a Family Camping Trip Run Smoothly

    To help you make the most of your family camping experience, whether it’s your first trip or as a family, or you want things to go better this time around, we’ve got you covered with our tips to help make things run a little smoother for everyone. 

    #1 Be Prepared With Strong Camping Skills

    Having strong camping skills ensures that you can efficiently set up camp, handle unexpected challenges, and maintain a safe environment for children.

    Skills such as pitching tents, starting a fire, and navigating through the wilderness reduce stress and provide a structured experience, allowing you to focus on creating fun and engaging activities for the entire family.

    This preparedness translates to a smoother, more enjoyable camping trip for everyone involved.

    The best thing is that you don't need to have a wealth of camping experience to do this. Watching some YouTube vlogs or reading blogs like the JustSupplies blog can give you all the knowledge you need to nail camping!

    Knowing how to build a campfire will make your first evening under the stars much less stressful, too!

    #2 Invest in a Quality Family Tent

    Updating your old festival tent is a must if this is your first camping trip as a family! A quality family tent offers ample space and durability, ensuring comfort and protection against the elements.

    With multiple compartments, it accommodates privacy needs and varying schedules, preventing disturbances.

    Reliable materials and sturdy construction withstand weather conditions, providing a safe haven.

    Best Family Camping Tents
    Shop now

    #3 Be Prepared for All Weather Conditions

    British summer weather is famously unpredictable, ranging from scorching sun to sudden downpours. By packing versatile clothing, waterproofs, and sun protection, you can stay comfortable no matter what the skies throw at you.

    A well-prepared camper anticipates these fluctuations, which reduces stress and keeps the family's spirits high.

    Being prepared for all weather means packing...

    • Sun cream
    • Hats
    • T-shirts
    • Raincoats
    • Wellies
    • Sandals
    • Extra blankets
    • Hoodies
    • Fans
    • Hand warmers
    Shop now

    #4 Pack to Create a Safe Home Away From Home

    Packing extra windbreaks and shelters can create a private, safe compound for the whole family to enjoy, regardless of the weather.

    These additions provide essential protection from strong winds, glaring sun, and unexpected rain, ensuring comfort and safety.

    They also help define a secure, private space where children can play freely and adults can relax, making your camping experience more enjoyable and stress-free.

    Shop now

    #5 Plan Your Camping Activities in Advance

    Planning activities in advance ensures that each day is filled with engaging and exciting pursuits, minimising downtime and preventing the dreaded "I'm bored" complaints.

    By having a variety of games, crafts, and explorations ready, you can keep children entertained and stimulated throughout the trip.

    This foresight reduces stress and creates a balanced itinerary that caters to everyone's interests, making it more enjoyable for the entire family.

    10 boredom-busting games to play when camping

    How to Keep Children Entertained When Camping

    One of the hardest parts of a camping holiday with children is keeping them entertained all day and into the evening.

    Of course, a lot of activities are weather-dependent, which can mean a lot of last-minute changes to the itinerary, so we've included activities for all weather types to help you pivot when you need to!

    General Camping Activities

    Assuming that the weather is going to be generally fine (not too hot, not too wet!), here's a list of general camping activities to keep everyone entertained during the day!

    1. Nature Scavenger Hunt: Create a list of items for the kids to find, like specific leaves, rocks, or animal tracks.
    2. Campfire Stories: Share spooky or funny stories around the campfire to spark imagination and bonding.
    3. Hiking Adventures: Explore nearby trails and let the kids lead the way using a map or compass.
    4. Stargazing: Bring a telescope or simply lie on blankets and identify constellations and planets.
    5. Outdoor Games: To keep energy levels high, play classic games like tag, hide-and-seek, or capture the flag.
    6. Geocaching: Engage in a modern treasure hunt using GPS devices to find hidden caches.
    7. Photography Expedition: Give the kids disposable or digital cameras to capture their favourite moments and nature scenes.
    8. Environmental Education: Teach children about local flora and fauna and the importance of conservation.

    Each of these activities can be tailored to fit the ages and interests of your children, ensuring that the entire family has a memorable and enjoyable camping experience.

    Wet Weather Activities

    The weather during British summertime has just as much chance of being a washout as it does of being glorious sunshine, so our tips and tricks couldn't be without some wet weather activities for the whole family.

    1. Rainy Day Crafts: Bring along some craft supplies like coloured paper, markers, glue, and stickers. Creating nature-themed art or DIY jewellery can keep kids busy and creative even when it’s pouring outside.
    2. Board Games and Puzzles: Pack a few favourite board games or puzzles to enjoy indoors. They are great for family bonding and can keep everyone engaged during a rainy day.
    3. Story Time: A collection of favourite books or story audiobooks can be a lifesaver. Reading together or listening to stories can be comforting and enjoyable while huddled inside a tent.
    4. Indoor Scavenger Hunts: Create an indoor scavenger hunt. Make use of the items around your tent or campsite, and give the kids a list of things to find or identify.
    5. Cooking Together: Use the downtime to cook or bake simple recipes. Making s'mores or preparing sandwiches together can be a fun and messy activity that breaks the monotony. See our list of 10 stress-free lunch ideas when camping with the kids!

    Hot Weather Activities

    Occasionally, our summers are baking hot, and it's almost too hot to do anything, especially when your options are out in the sun or in a hot tent, but that doesn't stop kids from wanting to be entertained!

    Here are some suggestions to keep kids entertained but cool on a hot camping trip!

    1. Water Play: Bring along water balloons, squirt guns, or even a small inflatable pool to keep kids cool and entertained during hot weather.
    2. Nature Exploration: Go for a family hike, encouraging children to identify plants, insects, and animals. Equip them with magnifying glasses or binoculars for a more immersive experience.
    3. Craft Time: Use natural materials like leaves, sticks, and stones to create art projects or build mini forts.
    4. Treasure Hunts: Organise a treasure hunt with clues hidden around the campsite. Use small toys or treats as treasures for the kids to find.
    5. Solar-Powered Projects: Engage the kids with solar-powered experiments, like a solar oven or a DIY solar-powered toy. These activities keep them busy and teach them about renewable energy.

    By planning for different weather conditions and a range of activities, you can keep your children entertained and happy throughout your camping trip, no matter the weather.

    Tricks for Avoiding Tantrums In the Campground

    No matter how old your children are, there's always the risk of a tantrum or two, but don't let that put you off the idea! There are things you can do to help avoid tantrums in the campground.

    Tip Description

    Maintain Routine

    Stick to your child's usual meal and nap times for a sense of security.

    Bring Comfort Items

    Pack familiar items like a favourite blanket or stuffed animal for reassurance.

    Keep Snacks Accessible

    Pack healthy food and snacks to prevent hunger-induced meltdowns.

    Plan Short Activities

    Plan short, engaging activities with frequent breaks to avoid overwhelming toddlers.

    Involve Kids in Decisions

    Give toddlers choices like picking snacks or activities to reduce frustration.

    Involve Kids in Camp Activities

    Let them help with age-appropriate tasks like collecting kindling, or preparing meals.

    Use Positive Reinforcement

    Praise good behaviour to encourage a positive camping experience.

    Create a Quiet Space

    Designate a calming space like a small tent with pillows and blankets.

    Prepare for Downtime

    Pack quiet activities like books, colouring supplies, or quiet toys.

    Stay Patient and Calm

    Remain calm during tantrums to de-escalate the situation and model emotional management.

    Implementing these strategies can minimise the chances of tantrums and ensure a happier, smoother camping experience for your entire family.

    Choose a Camping Style That Works for You!

    This is our number one top tip for camping with kids! 

    We all have an image in our head of what we want our perfect family camping trip to look like, filled with laughter, s'mores, campfires, and being off grid, but that doesn't always work out.

    Part of having kids is going with the flow and changing your plans. If it's too hot or too wet to go out and do things, it's okay to resort to tablets and phones for entertainment in the shade, even if it means breaking your screen time rules!

    If your children don't take to the great outdoors like you'd hoped on their first camping trip, it's okay to head further afield to towns for regular entertainment like movies and shopping. It's even okay if you decide to sack it all off and head home early.

    Ultimately, the main goal of a holiday is to ensure that you're having a good time, and if that means you have to go glamping instead of camping, it'll be worth it for the memories.

    Explore the 45 best campsites in England by region to find a location that works for you!

    Key Takeaways: Top Tips for School Holiday Camping with Children

    Planning the perfect camping trip for your family is something that many of us dream of, and even though it can be difficult to execute, it's not impossible.

    With our helpful tips, tricks, and hacks, you can ensure your whole family creates lasting memories on your camping trip, and the adults can survive the school holidays a little easier!

    Don't forget to check out our Essential Family Camping Checklist to make sure you have everything you need and don’t forget to pack any of the essentials!

Buy too small a tarp, and it won’t cover your tent or camp set up. But buy too large a tarp, and you’ll add unnecessary weight to your kit (and nobody wants to lug around extra weight on a camping trip). So what size tarp is right for your camping trip?

Tarps can largely vary in size and shape depending on the type of tarp it is, the materials it's made from, and the number of configurations it can be set up in. 

But, most importantly, you want the tarp to fully cover whatever area you want to shelter on your trip, whether that be over a tent, hung over a sleeping bag, or as a roof for a camping kitchen.

To help you find out what size tarp is right for your camping trip, we’ve got a rundown of all the things you need to think about, as well as the most common tarp sizes.

    What is the Best Size for a Tarp?

    When choosing the right tarp size for your camping trip, consider what you need to cover and how you’ll use it. 

    A good rule of thumb is to select a tarp at least 0.5m longer and wider than the area you want to cover. For example, a 2x2.5m tarp usually works well for a 2-person tent. For extra coverage for gear or larger groups, a 3x3.5m tarp might be better.

    If using a tarp as a standalone shelter or hammock cover, you might need different dimensions. A 3x3m or 3x4.5m tarp offers ample protection from rain and wind while ensuring comfort. 

    Larger tarps, like 3.5x6m, are great for communal areas or kitchen spaces, sheltering multiple people and equipment.

    Ultimately, the best tarp size depends on your specific needs. Evaluate your camping setup and choose a tarp that ensures both lightness in your pack and adequate protection from the elements.

    We’ve outlined the most common tarp sizes below, along with our recommendations for each…

    Bikepacker Tarp

    For bikepackers, the ideal tarp size balances lightweight portability and ample coverage. A 2.5x3m tarp is typically optimal, providing sufficient shelter for both the bike and the rider without adding excessive weight.

    This size ensures you can comfortably cover your sleeping area and protect your bike from the elements.

    Given the compact and minimalist nature of bikepacking, it’s essential to choose a tarp that packs small yet offers robust protection. This will ensure a comfortable and dry camp set up after a day of cycling adventures.

    Made from 190T polyester, this simple tarp is fully waterproof to keep you sheltered all night.

    2x2 Tarp: Bikepacking & Hiking

    A 2x2m tarp is ideal for bikepacking and hiking trips due to its compactness and versatility. This size effectively provides sufficient coverage for solo campers, ensuring protection from the elements while keeping the gear lightweight.

    Its small footprint makes it easy to pack and carry, which is crucial for bikepackers and hikers who need to minimise weight and space.

    Additionally, a 2x2m tarp can serve multiple purposes, from shelter to ground cover, offering flexibility in various camping conditions.

    The simplicity and efficiency of this tarp size make it perfect for those who value both functionality and ease on their outdoor adventures.

    This tarp's dark olive green colour makes it ideal for woodland and forest camping, making it suitable for a wide range of adventures. Made from 190T polyester, this tarp can withstand even the roughest conditions for multiple trips.

    You can set this tarp up in an A-frame or diamond shelter for maximum protection from the elements. 

    It also makes a fantastic shelter for the DD Junior Frontline Hammock!

    2x3 Tarp: 1-Person

    This tarp provides slightly more coverage than its square counterpart, making it ideal for solo campers who like a bit more room to spread out. This size provides sufficient shelter to protect against the elements while leaving space for essential items like backpacks and cooking equipment.

    Its versatility allows it to be set up in various configurations, such as an A-frame or lean-to, ensuring optimal protection and comfort.

    Compact and lightweight, a 2x3m tarp can be easily packed, making it perfect for those prioritising mobility and efficiency on their solo camping adventures.

    This tarp is the ideal option for solo campers who are looking for a quality product with a little more room. Made from durable 2,500mm waterproof Silnylon with a micro ripstop pattern, you can be sure you'll be protected from whatever the weather throws at you.

    Despite being a compact piece of kit, this tarp is versatile in its applications. Whether you need ground cover, a protective rain cover, or a shelter on uneven ground, this tarp has got you covered.

    Weighing only 340g in total, this tarp won't weigh you down on your hike to your campsite or take up a lot of room in your kit.

    3x3 (or 3.5x3.5) Tarp: 1-2 Persons

    A 3m x 3m tarp is ideal for 1-2 persons, providing ample coverage for a comfortable shelter. This size is perfect for protecting against the elements while ensuring enough space for sleeping and minimal gear. 

    A tarp of this size can also be set up in various configurations, such as an A-frame or Diamond configuration, making it a versatile choice for different camping scenarios.

    If you need additional room for more camping equipment or extra comfort, a 3.5x3.5m tarp offers expanded coverage. 

    It allows you to keep your gear dry and within reach without feeling cramped, making it a versatile choice for couples or solo campers who prefer a bit more space.
