    This tarp (33% larger than its 3mx3m counterpart) is ideal for dual camping trips, whether you're a couple or with a friend. Its larger size allows you to pitch a tarp shelter in a wider range of configurations without sacrificing ground coverage.

    As well as the size being a bonus, the multi-camo print helps you blend into your surroundings no matter where you're camping, making it ideal for stealth or wild camping adventures as well as nature spotting day trips.

    XL Tarp: 3-Persons or Small Groups

    An XL tarp, typically measuring around 4.5x3m, is perfect for covering 3 people or small groups. This size ensures ample space for sleeping areas, essential gear, and even communal activities, all while providing robust protection against the elements.

    Its larger dimensions allow it to be set up in various configurations, such as an A-frame or extended canopy, ensuring comfort and versatility for any camping scenario.

    Whether you're camping with family or friends, an XL tarp ensures everyone stays dry and comfortable.

    Our Recommendation: DD Tarp XL

    Shop now

    DD Hammocks are leaders in durable camping tarp production, and their XL tarp is no different. 

    Measuring a generous 4.5mx3m, this tarp can easily cover a campsite of three people or more. Its versatile 19 attachment points allow for multiple configurations, ensuring maximum coverage and comfort.

    Made from 190T polyester with a waterproof rating of 3,000mm, this tarp will withstand harsh weather conditions while keeping you and your gear dry and protected. 

    Best of all, this tarp is available in a variety of colours to suit your camping preferences.

    5x5 Tarp: Group Shelter

    A 5x5m tarp is ideal as a group shelter because it provides substantial coverage, ensuring there’s enough space for multiple campers and their gear.

    This large footprint allows for a versatile setup, such as an A-frame or a communal canopy, which can shelter a group from rain, wind, and sun.

    The generous dimensions mean you can create a comfortable shared area for socialising, cooking, or group activities, all while keeping everything dry and protected.

    Additionally, despite its size, many 5mx5m tarps are made from lightweight and durable materials, ensuring that they won't be too cumbersome to pack and carry. This makes it perfect for family trips, DofE groups, or any group camping adventure.

    Our Recommendation: DD Tarp 5 x 5 

    Shop now

    With enough space to cover an entire outdoor community, the 5x5m tarp from DD Hammocks is ideal for campers who travel in large groups or people who run outdoor events.

    With 25 reinforced attachment points, 9 of which are central, there are multiple set-up options to help you adapt to your environment and provide shelter for your whole group no matter where you are.

    Of course, this tarp is waterproof rated to 3,000mm, to keep your camp or activity dry and sheltered from the elements.

    How Much Bigger Should a Tarp Be Than a Tent?

    To ensure proper coverage, a tarp should be at least 2 feet longer and wider than your tent. This extra area effectively protects against rain and wind by creating an overhang that prevents water from seeping into your tent.

    Of course, if you're using the tarp as an additional groundsheet for your tent, the tarp should actually be a little smaller than the footprint of your tent to prevent water from pooling underneath it. If you have a large tarp already, you can fold it to create an effective groundsheet.

    What Size Tarp for a Rain Fly?

    Tent Capacity Floor Size Tarp Size

    When selecting a tarp to use as a rainfly for your tent, it is crucial to choose one that is both longer and wider than the tent itself. This ensures that the tarp provides adequate coverage, extending beyond the edges of the tent to protect against rain and other elements.

    A larger tarp will create a protective overhang, helping to keep your tent dry by preventing water from seeping in.

    What Size Tarp to Use Under a Tent

    To determine the appropriate tarp size for use as a ground sheet, you'll need to measure your tent's footprint. This footprint is the area that the base of your tent will cover when it's set up.

    Once you have the dimensions of the tent’s floor, you can use the following formula:

    Tarp size under tent = Tent footprint size

    For example, if your tent’s footprint measures 7 feet by 5 feet, you should select a tarp that matches these dimensions as closely as possible. It’s essential that the tarp does not extend far beyond the tent’s base to avoid water pooling under the tent.

    For the best results, ensure that the tarp edges are just slightly within the tent's boundary to keep the groundsheet functional and effective in preventing moisture from getting inside.

    This precise fit will provide a protective layer between the tent floor and the ground, enhancing your camping experience by keeping the tent floor dry and clean.

    Find out more about tent footprints with our guide for campers!

    Key Takeaways: Getting Your Tarp Size Right

    Choosing the right tarp size is crucial for a comfortable and hassle-free camping trip. A properly sized tarp offers enough protection from rain, wind, and sun to keep you dry and safe. It also provides adequate space for your group and gear without adding unnecessary weight or bulk.

    Conversely, a poorly sized tarp can result in inadequate coverage, discomfort, and extra trouble, ruining your camping experience. So, picking the right tarp size is essential for a successful and enjoyable outdoor adventure.

Struggling to figure out what type of tarp you need for your camping trip? We’ve got you covered (literally!) with our guide below.

Whether you’re headed off on a stealthy wild camping trip to be at one with nature, or you’re planning a camping weekend with friends, a tarp is a great bit of kit to take with you – especially when none of us know what the glorious British weather will do!

But with so many different types of tarps and setups to choose from, it can be tricky to know which type you need for your specific trip. 

So, to help make your decision a little easier, we’ve put together a quick rundown of the different tarp types and setups available.

          Things to Look Out For When Buying a Camping Tarp

          When buying a tarp for your next camping trip, there are a few things to look out for. Here are the top things we look for in a tarp when we're upgrading our gear.

          • Waterproofing: Ensure the tarp is fully waterproof to keep you dry during rain showers.
          • UV Protection: Look for a tarp with UV protection to shield you from harmful UV rays.
          • Size: Consider the size of the tarp relative to your needs; larger tarps provide more coverage.
          • Shape: Different shapes offer varying levels of protection and setup options, such as rectangular or hexagonal.
          • Material: Examine the material for durability, weight, and resistance to wear and tear.
          • Reinforced Eyelets: Check for reinforced eyelets or grommets for secure and easy attachment.
          • Weight: Opt for a lightweight tarp if you need to carry it on long hikes or backpacking trips.
          • Packability: Ensure it can be packed down small for efficient storage and transport.
          • Versatility: Look for a tarp that can be set up in multiple configurations to suit different conditions and needs.

          You can treat this list as a checklist to compare different tarps to in order to make an informed decision!

          What Type of Tarp to Use When Camping

          When building your pack for your next camping trip, you can choose from multiple different types of tarps, which can be pretty overwhelming if you're a beginner. 

          We've outlined the different types of tarps and their most useful uses to help you make an informed decision.

          A Flat Tarp

          A flat tarp is a versatile and essential piece of camping gear for any outdoor enthusiast.

          Unlike tarps designed with specific shapes or configurations, a flat tarp is simply a rectangular or square sheet with grommets or tie-out points around the edges, offering the freedom to set it up in numerous ways depending on the camper's needs and the environment.

          Uses of a flat tarp when camping:

          • Shelter: Can be pitched in various configurations to create a rain or sun shelter.
          • Ground Cover: Acts as a moisture barrier when laid on the ground beneath a tent or sleeping bag.
          • Windbreak: Useful as a wind barrier when set up on one side of a campsite.
          • Cooking Area Cover: Provides a protective covering over cooking gear to shield from rain or dew.
          • Gear Protection: Can be used to cover and protect camping gear from the elements.
          • Hammock Rain Fly: When rigged above a hammock, it provides protection from rain.

          Our Recommendation…

          Our recommendation for a flat tarp is the DD Superlight XL tarp. As the name suggests, this tarp is extra large, measuring 4.5m x 2.9m. This is big enough to create a dry area between tents or provide day shelter for your whole group of campers, ideal for scouts or D of E trips.

          Made from ripstop nylon with 3,000mm PU waterproof coating, this lightweight tarp will shelter you in all weather conditions.

          Shop now

          A Shaped Tarp

          Unlike a flat tarp, a shaped tarp is pre-cut and sewn into specific configurations to suit particular camping needs.

          These tarps often feature curved edges and tailored panels, which allow for more specialised setups and efficient coverage.

          The design typically simplifies the process of pitching the tarp, making it quicker and more intuitive for campers.

          Uses of a shaped tarp when camping:

          • Tent Replacement or Addition: Can be used as a lightweight alternative to a tent, offering shelter with less weight to carry. It can also be used in conjunction with a tent to create additional living space.
          • Rain Shelter: Its pre-designed shape makes it particularly effective at funnelling rainwater away, providing better protection during heavy rain.
          • Snow Shelter: The specific configurations of a shaped tarp are advantageous in winter camping conditions, serving as a barrier against wind and snow.
          • Privacy Screen: Its shape can easily be adjusted to serve as a privacy screen around campsites or portable toilets.
          • Enhanced Aerodynamics: Designed to reduce wind resistance, allowing it to remain stable and secure even in strong winds.

          Shaped tarps offer enhanced functionality and convenience, making them a favourite among seasoned campers who value both performance and ease of use.

          Our Recommendation…

          Our recommendation for a shaped tarp has to be the OneWind Dyad Lightweight Shelter. This versatile shelter can be erected in a range of formations to provide adequate protection from wind and rain on your trip.

          Ideal for stealth camping, this survival shelter can shield you and your gear from wind and rain without weighing your pack down at only 265g! 

          Made from durable Silnylon, you can be sure this shelter has your back on any terrain.

          Shop now

          Tarp Tents

          A tarp tent is a minimalist and lightweight shelter option that blends the features of a traditional tent and tarp. It provides more protection and structural integrity than a flat or shaped tarp alone but is less cumbersome than a regular tent.

          Tarp tents often consist of a shaped or flat tarp combined with a simple framework, such as trekking poles, guy lines, and stakes, to form a tent-like structure.

          This offers campers a versatile and efficient shelter solution without the bulk and weight of a traditional tent.

          Differences between a Tarp Tent & a Regular Tent:

          Feature Tarp Tent Regular Tent

          Weight

          Lighter

          Heavier

          Setup

          Versatile, improvised

          Built-in poles, specific instructions

          Packability

          Packs down smaller

          Takes up more space

          Ventilation

          Better ventilation

          Less ventilation, prone to condensation

          Versatility

          Configurable for different conditions

          Fixed shape and setup

          Cost

          More economical

          More expensive

          Overall, tarp tents offer a flexible, lightweight, and cost-effective shelter solution, appealing especially to those who prioritise mobility and adaptability in their camping gear.

          Our Recommendation…

          Our recommendation for a durable tarp tent is the OneWind Blackthorn Ultralight. This structured tent is incredibly lightweight, at only 1.9kg, and big enough to shelter 3-4 standing adults. 

          Made from durable Silnylon fabric, it will last you through multiple trips. But the main thing we love about this tent is the doors on either end, which provide additional protection from the elements and allow you to regulate temperature on your trip. 

          Shop now

          What Materials Should a Tarp Be Made From?

          The ideal tarp material should be durable, lightweight, and weather-resistant. Popular options include

          • Silnylon – this silicone and nylon blend is known for its strength and waterproofing.
          • Ripstop nylon – valued for its quality tear resistance.
          • Polypropylene – appreciated for its affordability, water resistance, and chemical resistance. Polypropylene tarps are often used for temporary shelters and ground covers.
          • Polyethylene – recognised for its high durability and excellent water resistance. Polyethylene tarps are commonly used for long-term covers and heavy-duty ground covers.

          Choosing the right material depends on your specific camping needs and conditions, but these options provide a good starting point for any outdoor adventure.

          What is the Strongest Tarp Material?

          The strongest tarp material is ripstop nylon. Known for its exceptional tear resistance and durability, it is ideal for enduring harsh weather conditions and heavy usage and providing reliable protection during outdoor activities.

          Are Polypropylene or Polyethylene Tarps Better?

          When camping, neither polypropylene nor polyethylene tarps are inherently better; it depends on your needs.

          Polypropylene tarps are lightweight, affordable, and water-resistant, suitable for short-term use like temporary shelters or ground covers. However, they're generally less durable and less UV-resistant than polyethylene tarps.

          Polyethylene tarps are highly durable and water-resistant, ideal for long-term use and heavy-duty applications like rain shelters or gear protection. They also offer better UV resistance for prolonged outdoor exposure but are heavier and less packable than polypropylene tarps.

          For campers, the choice between polypropylene and polyethylene tarps can be difficult. We recommend changing tack altogether and opting for a lightweight, durable, water-resistant Silnylon or Ripstop nylon tarp instead.

          Does It Matter What Colour a Tarp Is?

          The colour of your tarp matters more than you'd think! It's more than just choosing a colour that you like, you need to take into account the type of camping you're doing and the environment you'll be camping in.

          If you're attempting to wild camp or stealth camp, you'll need to choose a tarp that blends in with the environment you'll be camping in.

          • Forest Camping = Green tarps
          • Woodland Camping = Brown tarps
          • Variable Environments = Multi Camo tarps

          Of course, if you're camping at a campsite or a festival, the colour of your tarp matters much less in terms of helping you blend into your surroundings.

          What is the Best Thickness for a Tarp?

          Balancing weight and durability is one of the hardest parts of buying a tarp for a camping trip, especially if you're hiking.

          That said, we'd say that the thickness of your tarp should be slightly more important than its weight to ensure it properly protects you.

          The ideal thickness for a tarp typically ranges from 5 to 12 mils (0.005 to 0.012 inches).

          Thicker tarps obviously offer enhanced durability and weather resistance, making them suitable for rugged conditions, while thinner tarps are lighter and more portable, ideal for backpacking and light camping.

          You should choose the thickness of your tarp based on your needs, focusing on the terrain and weather conditions you'll be camping in.

          Key Takeaways: What Type of Tarp to Use for Camping

          There are various types of tarps available, each offering unique benefits for camping. Flat tarps provide versatile shelter options, shaped tarps offer specialised configurations, and tarp tents combine lightweight features with structural integrity.

A new year is upon us, and that means it's time to plan your adventures for the next 12 months. We've made things easier for you with our guide to the essential outdoor gear you need for a fun 2025!

We've covered the basics of camping, plus the little extras that we know people tend to forget.

So, whether you're new to camping and committing to your New Year's resolution, or you're a seasoned pro looking to update your camping supplies for a big camping trip, we've got you covered!

The Best Multi-Season Tents

Investing in a quality tent suitable for multiple seasons can vastly improve the comfort and convenience of your camping adventures in 2025.

A multi-season tent is designed to withstand varying weather conditions, ensuring protection against rain, wind, and even light snowfall. This versatility means you can enjoy camping trips throughout the year without the need for several different tents.

Our Top Sleeping Pads & Pillows

As we dive into a new year full of adventures, let's face it: we're not getting any younger! Comfort during our outdoor escapades can make all the difference.

For 2025, investing in quality sleeping pads and pillows is a must to guarantee a good night's sleep after a day of excitement.

A comfy sleeping pad gives you the support and insulation you need from the ground, helping to avoid those annoying aches and pains.

Pair it with a supportive pillow, and you've got the neck and head cushioning you need for proper rest, making your camping trips more fun and refreshing.

Our Favourite Stove & Cookware Kit

Cooking while camping can be a real treat, especially if you've got a trusty stove and some sturdy cookware.

In 2025, having quality cooking gear will make your outdoor cooking a breeze, helping you whip up hot meals easily.

A good stove means quick and easy heating, perfect for those chilly mornings and cool evenings. Pair it with reliable cookware, and you'll cut down on any hassle, allowing more time to enjoy the great outdoors.

Whether you're heating expedition meals or cooking lunches from scratch, the right tools turn cooking into a fun part of your camping trip, not just a chore.

Top-Rated Multi-Functional Sleeping Bag

When considering essential outdoor gear for 2025, multi-functional sleeping bags stand out as a smart investment. These innovative sleeping solutions offer versatility and convenience that cater to a variety of needs and conditions.

Multi-functional sleeping bags are designed to adapt effortlessly to different situations, allowing you to get more use from a single piece of equipment.

For example, sleeping bags that double as ponchos provide warmth and protection both during rest and as outerwear, making them perfect for unpredictable weather or multi-functional needs during your adventures.

These designs enhance your camping experience, ensuring comfort and agility without the bulk.

The Most Comfortable Hiking Boots

Investing in comfortable hiking boots is essential for any planned adventures in 2025, as they are the foundation of a successful trek.

Quality hiking boots are your best friend when it comes to support and stability, keeping those pesky sprains or blisters at bay that can totally ruin a fun outing.

Plus, comfy boots cut down on fatigue by offering cushioning and shock absorption, letting you go the extra mile with less stress on your feet and joints.

Picking the right hiking boots can really boost your adventure, giving you the confidence to explore the great outdoors without any hassle.

Versatile Lighting Solutions

Lighting options like torches and head torches are a must-have for any camping trip, giving you the light you need for all sorts of situations.

They keep things safe and convenient out there, whether you're finding your way along a trail, setting up a tent after dark, or just looking for something in your bag.

Head torches, in particular, are super handy since they let you move around or work in the dark while keeping your hands free.

Plus, modern torches come with cool features like adjustable brightness, strobe settings, and long battery life, making them great for everything from emergencies to the usual campsite activities.

The Smaller Essentials to Remember

Of course, it's not just about the main bits of your kit. There are smaller essentials that can make or break your trip if they're forgotten or, worse, broken!

Here are some of our top recommendations for rounding out your camping kit for 2025 and into the future!

A Full First Aid Kit

A full first aid kit is a crucial component of any camping or outdoor adventure, as it equips you to handle minor injuries and emergencies efficiently.

Whether you're dealing with cuts, scrapes, insect bites, or even more serious issues like sprains or burns, having the right supplies on hand can prevent complications and keep a situation from escalating.

A well-stocked kit not only provides immediate relief but also gives you the confidence and peace of mind to tackle unexpected challenges.

You can always build your own first aid kit with stuff you have at home, but we prefer a pre-stocked one with everything we might need.

For larger trips, we love the comprehensive Elite Explorer's Kit from BCB. If you're just going for a hike, the Kombat UK Small First Aid Kit should be fine.

Weatherproof Clothing

Weatherproof clothing is a must-have for a comfy and fun trip, keeping you dry and warm no matter the weather. Nature can be unpredictable, switching from sunny to rainy or windy in minutes.

Good weatherproof gear protects you from rain and wind, saving you from discomfort and any health risks from being wet or chilled too long.

Plus, it often comes with breathable materials to keep your body temperature just right so you don’t overheat or get sweaty.

Sun Protection (Yes, Even in the UK!)

Sun protection is paramount all year round, even in the UK, where the weather is often gloomy yet surprisingly deceptive when it comes to UV exposure.

While it may seem that the sun's rays are less potent during the colder months or on overcast days, harmful UV rays can still penetrate clouds and reach your skin.

Items like sunscreen, hats, sunglasses, UV-protective clothing and camping tarps are essential parts of your outdoor gear, ensuring your skin is safeguarded no matter the season or weather conditions.

A Comfortable Backpack for Your Equipment

Having a comfy, roomy backpack or rucksack is key for hikes and camping trips. It makes sure you can carry all your gear without sacrificing comfort or risking health issues.

Car camping can be a great way to try out camping, especially if you're not totally sold on the idea of sleeping amongst nature! But there are still things you need to make it a good trip, which is where our ultimate car camping essentials list comes in handy!

While you don't have to make many big purchases, like a tent or shelter, there are still some essential bits of kit you'll need to make your car camping adventure comfortable and safe.

Basic Essentials for Car Camping Checklist

There are a few basic essentials you're going to need to make your car camping trip more than just a cramped night in the backseat of your car.

Here are the top car camping essentials you should have to make your camping trip fun and comfortable!

1. A Working Car

It might seem obvious, but having a reliable car is a must for any car camping adventure. Your car is your transport, storage, and even your sleeping spot, so it's super important for the trip.

Before you head out, make sure your ride is in good shape with basic car maintenance. Give the brakes, fluids, lights, and tyres a once-over to avoid any road surprises.

A well-maintained car means you can kick back and enjoy the great outdoors without any hiccups. If your car's not up to par, those camping plans could hit a snag fast!

2. Sleeping Pad or Air Mattress

Creating a comfortable sleeping space in your car is key for a good night's rest on a camping adventure. That's why a sleeping pad or an air mattress is a must-have.

They add extra cushioning and insulation against the car's hard, cold surface, helping you wake up refreshed and ready for the day – crucially avoiding a stiff neck that ruins your hike!

Whether you pick a compact sleeping mat or a more sturdy air mattress designed for the back of your car, both give you the comfort and support you need.

3. Sleeping Bag & Camping Pillow

To round out your car camping sleep setup, don't forget a sleeping bag and a camping pillow. These are key for staying warm and comfy, letting you crash peacefully after a day of adventure.

Your sleeping bag will keep you warm when the temperature drops at night, and a camping pillow gives your neck the support it needs.

Sure, you could bring a regular pillow, but be warned – it might get damp from car condensation, which isn’t great for a good night's sleep. A camping pillow, made just for outdoor conditions, helps dodge that issue, keeping your sleep space dry.

The Deluxe Air camping pillow from Highlander practically guarantees a great night's sleep whether you're in a car or a tent, while the Snowbird Mummy duck down winter sleeping bag from NatureHike will keep you toasty in all seasons!

4. Reliable Camping Stove

A trusty camping stove is a game-changer for dining during car camping trips. You can enjoy hot, tasty meals wherever you park for the night. There's nothing like a warm cup of coffee or camp meals under the stars after exploring nature.

A camping stove lets you cook various dishes and boil water for cleaning or soup. It's portable and efficient and is easy to set up and use in any weather.

Whether you're a gourmet camp chef or prefer simple meals, the right gas or solid-fuel stove boosts your culinary options while camping.

Consider the Petrel G3 Ultralight Cooking system from Fire Maple Gear, known for its durability and ease of use, to keep delicious meals close at hand.

Find Your Ideal Camping Stove From JustSupplies

5. Food Cooler

Taking a food cooler on your car camping trip is a must for keeping your cooking supplies fresh and safe to eat.

Whether you're bringing along some pre-made meals, snacks, or just a few cold drinks, a cooler will keep all your camping food chilled and tasty.

The Catago Box 50 Camp Cooking Transport Bag from PetroMax is a great option that fits plenty of sustenance for your trip. Or, if you want to keep things simple, the 27L Cooler Backpack is an ideal option that can conveniently be taken on a hike with you!

Keep Things Cool With Our Range of Camping Coolers

6. Toiletries & Personal Items

Don't forget to pack your toiletries and personal items for your car camping adventure! These essentials keep you fresh, hygienic and comfortable while you're out there.

Make sure you've got the basics like a toothbrush, toothpaste, and biodegradable soap, plus other hygiene must-haves like deodorant and wet wipes. Trash bags are also super handy!

Think about what you need specifically – any meds, skincare stuff, or personal items you can't live without.

7. Portable Charger & Torches

No camping trip is complete without some gadgets and gizmos! So, don't forget to pack a portable charger and some torches for your car camping trip!

A portable charger is a lifesaver for keeping your devices powered up so you can snap photos, use GPS, or reach out in an emergency.

As for torches, they're super handy for those late-night bathroom runs or finding your way around the campsite after dark. 

Go for a reliable torch with a long battery life, like the TrustFire WF-502B. Rechargeable ones can be pretty convenient, too. With these tools, you'll stay connected and navigate the outdoors safely!

Light Your Way With Our Range of Camping Torches

8. A First Aid Kit

Having a well-stocked first aid or survival kit is a must for any camping trip – it's a key part of your gear.

Nature can be unpredictable, and accidents can happen, whether it's a minor cut or something more serious.

A good first aid kit lets you handle these situations calmly and efficiently so small problems don't turn into big ones.

To make things easier, you can purchase pre-stocked first aid kits like the BCB Adventure Survival Tin or the BCB Personal Safety Kit, which are ideal for first-time campers. Just remember to restock the things you use!

Check Out Our Complete Camping First Aid Kit Checklist

Winter Car Camping Essentials

If you're planning on taking a car camping trip in the winter (you're braver than most!), there are a few extra things you should be taking with you to ensure you're not shivering in your sleeping bag all night.

Here are some winter camping gear essentials for your trip!

1. Window Covers

Window covers are a must-have for your winter car camping trip. They do a great job of blocking out the morning sun if you want to sleep in, and they also insulate the glass.

This insulation keeps your car warmer by stopping heat from escaping through the windows during those chilly nights.

Think of window covers as an extra layer between you and the cold outside. They really make a difference, ensuring you can enjoy a warm and comfortable sleep without freezing.

2. Weather-Appropriate Clothing

Make sure you pack plenty of thermal tops, fleece jackets, and waterproof layers – these can be the difference between a miserable and enjoyable trip. The great thing about layering is that you can easily adjust your outfit to suit the changing weather or if you get sweaty on a hike.

Don’t forget thermal socks, gloves, and a warm hat because your extremities are usually the first to get chilly.

With the right clothes, you’ll be all set to enjoy your winter camping adventure without freezing!

3. Hand Warmers & Hot Water Bottles

When the temperature drops at night, hand warmers and hot water bottles are lifesavers. These handy items help you stay warm and comfy during those chilly evenings.

Hand warmers are super portable, so you can just slip them into your pockets or gloves to keep your fingers from freezing.

As for hot water bottles, they’re perfect for adding a touch of warmth inside your sleeping bag or on your lap while you kick back and relax.

With these essentials, you’re all set for a warm and toasty night's sleep, ready to recharge for another day of winter fun.

Discover Our Top Tips for Wild Camping in the Winter

4. A Camping Kettle

A portable kettle is a must-have for any winter car camping trip. It's a simple, effective way to fill up your hot water bottle and brew up warm drinks.

With a camping kettle, you can quickly boil water, so you've always got hot water at your fingertips for camp cooking.

Whether you're brewing a cup of tea to savour the crisp morning air or filling up your hot water bottle before bed, a trusty camping kettle is a winter camping essential.

Never Miss Your Morning Coffee With Our Range of Camping Kettles

5. Spare Dry Clothes

When you're getting ready to sleep in your car during the winter, having spare dry clothes is a lifesaver for staying warm.

All that sweat and condensation can build up during the day's outdoor activities, especially if you've been on the move, making your clothes damp and pretty useless at keeping you insulated.

No one wants a chilly night, right? So, switch into some dry clothes before jumping into your sleeping bag.

It's a simple trick, but it stops that cold, clammy feeling damp clothes can cause, helping to keep your tent dry and you to keep a steady body temperature.

Top Tips for Getting Car Camping Essentials on a Budget

When preparing for your first car camping adventure, it's possible to gather all the essential items without breaking the bank.

Here are some savvy tips to help you get set up for less:

By using what you have, borrowing from others, or strategically purchasing, you can easily gather your car camping essentials while staying within your budget.

How to Camp in Your Car

Car camping can sound like the ideal compromise for people who want to try camping but don't want to have to pitch a tent and shelter when they get to their campsite.

However, there's still a fair amount of work that needs to go into preparing for these trips.

Our Basic Car Camping Gear Setup

There's no single way to set up your car for a car camping trip, and every car is different in size and seat folding options, so it's often a matter of trial and error. 

Is Car Camping Legal in the UK?

Car camping legality varies across the UK, depending on location and local laws.

In many places, it's illegal to camp in your car on public roads and in certain parks. However, some designated areas and private lands allow it with permission.

Always check local regulations and landowner restrictions before setting up for the night.

Scotland permits wild camping more freely, but it's advisable to follow the "Leave No Trace" principles everywhere.

Final Thoughts: Pack the Essentials With Our Car Camping Checklist

Our essential car camping checklist is your go-to guide for a hassle-free adventure. It covers everything you need for a comfy trip, from sleeping gear to kitchen basics.

Stick to this list, and you won't forget any must-haves, ensuring your car camping experience is smooth and fun.

Pack smart and enjoy the great outdoors with peace of mind, knowing you're all set!

Quality tents are an investment, and knowing how long they last and how to properly care for them is crucial to deciding whether to invest in quality or opt for cheaper models. So, how long do tents last?

While tents do not have a set expiration date, some average lifespans can help inform your decision when purchasing a new one for your outdoor adventures.

With plenty of experience with all types of tents, we’ve put together some tips and advice to help you make your tent last for many years.

How Long Should a Tent Last?

The lifespan of a tent varies depending on usage and care, but generally, a well-maintained tent can last 5-10 years.

Proper maintenance includes regular cleaning, ensuring dry storage, avoiding sun exposure, and repairing minor tent damages promptly to maximise longevity.

Quality materials also influence durability…

What Are Tents Made Of? How to Choose the Best Material

Canvas Tents

Canvas tents are famous for being tough and usually outlast synthetic ones. With the right care, they can last 10 to 20 years or even more.

A few things can affect how long they last. Regular maintenance is super important – like making sure the tent is dry before you store it to avoid mould and mildew.

Applying a waterproof treatment also helps keep the fabric strong against the weather.

Even though canvas handles UV rays better than synthetic materials, too much sun can still wear it down over time.

Polyester Tents

Modern polyester tents are loved for being lightweight and affordable, which is why casual campers often pick them.

On average, these tents last around 3 to 7 years, depending on how often you use them and how well you take care of them.

Sunlight is their biggest enemy; UV rays can weaken the fibres over time, making them less strong and less waterproof. To help your tent last longer, try to set it up in the shade when you can or shelter it with a tarp.

Quality matters, too – tents made with better polyester and coatings are likely to last longer and withstand the elements better.

How Long Do Tents Stay Waterproof?

The waterproofness of tents depends on their material and usage frequency.

Polyester tents may start losing waterproof capability after 2-4 years of regular use, especially with frequent rain and UV exposure.

Canvas tents, however, hold their waterproofness longer due to their thicker fabric and the application of waterproof treatments.

Regular maintenance, such as reapplying waterproof coatings, repairing seams, and ensuring the tent is stored dry, can extend this timeframe for both canvas and polyester tents.

How to Make Your Tent Last Longer

Of course, these lifespans are just averages and estimates based on manufacturer guidelines and personal experiences with different tents over the years.

There's no reason why you can't make your tent or tarp shelter work harder for you by properly maintaining it.

Here are our top tips for how to make your tent last longer to get the most value for money.

How to Store Your Tent

Storing your tent properly is super important if you want it to last longer. Here are some things you should do before putting it away to make sure it lasts as long as possible:

When storing your tent, avoid cramming it into a tight space – this can stress the seams and fabric over time. Instead, try using a breathable storage sack instead of the original stuff sack for long-term storage.

To ensure it stays in great shape for years, keep it in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight and extreme temperatures.

Camping 101: 8 Tips to Stop Condensation in a Tent

How to Clean the Tent Body

Proper cleaning of your tent body is crucial for maintaining longevity for all types of tents, regardless of whether it's made from polyester or canvas.

Here's how you can do it for each material:

For a More Detailed Guide, Check Out How to Clean Your Tent in 6 Simple Steps

Regular cleaning, combined with proper storage practices, will ensure your tent remains in excellent condition for years of outdoor adventures.

Maintaining the Waterproofing of Your Tent

Keeping your tent waterproof is crucial for a comfortable and dry camping experience.

Over time, the factory-applied waterproof coatings on your tent can wear off, particularly if it's frequently used or exposed to harsh weather conditions. 

Here’s how you can maintain or restore your tent's waterproof capabilities:

By incorporating these practices into your tent care routine, you can extend its life and keep it performing at its best, ensuring dry and enjoyable camping trips.

How to Maintain Tent Poles

Maintaining fibreglass tent poles is essential to ensure they remain strong and reliable throughout your outdoor adventures. Here are some key steps you can take:

By following these maintenance tips and handling your fibreglass tent poles with care, you can ensure they remain in top condition and continue to provide sturdy support for your tent on all your camping excursions.

Replace Your Old or Worn Tent Poles With Top Outdoor Brands

What to Look for in a Quality Tent

When picking out a good tent, there are a few key things campers should think about to ensure a comfy and successful camping trip.

First, check out the tent's size and capacity to ensure it has enough room for everyone and their stuff.

Also, make sure the tent has the right season rating. 3-season tents work well for spring, summer and autumn, while 4-season tents are tougher for winter weather.

The material and durability of the tent matter a lot – look for fabrics like ripstop nylon or polyester with a strong waterproof coating to keep you protected and last longer.

Don't forget about ventilation; having some windows or vents can help cut down on condensation and keep things nice inside.

Think about the setup complexity, too. It's great to find a tent that's easy to pitch, especially if it comes with features like colour-coded poles and fewer parts. Having multiple entries and vestibules can make things more convenient, giving you extra space for your gear and making it easy to get in and out.

Finally, check out the tent's brand reputation and read some customer reviews to see what people are saying about its performance and durability. Just because it's an expensive tent, it doesn't mean it's a durable tent!

By focusing on these important aspects, you can pick a camping tent that'll give you reliability, protection, and comfort on your next outdoor adventure.

Explore Our Full Range of Tent & Tarp Accessories

Final Thoughts: Make Your Tent Last Longer With Proper Care

Keeping your tent in great shape is important to make sure you get the most bang for your buck! After each trip, clean it, store it in a cool, dry place, and use a footprint or groundsheet to protect against UV damage and wear.

If you follow these tips, your tent will be ready for more camping adventures!

What Size Tent for a Festival

We've included instructions on how to set up your hammock tent independently for day camps and sleeping under the stars in the summer, as well as how to incorporate a tarp to keep your hammock sheltered in more adverse weather conditions.

Whether you're a hammock tent newbie or just want to make sure you're pitching your hammock correctly, our tips and tricks are here to guide you!

How to Set Up a Hammock for Sleeping

Setting up your hammock so you can comfortably sleep in it is crucial for taking it on any camping trip beyond your own backyard.

Our guide includes using trees and other anchor points to help you practice setting up your hammock by itself in woodland and at UK campsites.

Step 1: Choose the Right Location

Before setting up your hammock, find a suitable location. Look for sturdy trees or anchor points about 12 to 15 feet apart.

Ensure the area is clear of hazards like sharp rocks or insect nests, and choose a spot that offers a slight incline for optimal drainage in case of rain.

Step 2: Secure the Straps or Ropes



Wrap tree-friendly straps or ropes around each tree or anchor point. Adjust them to about head height to ensure your hammock hangs at an ideal level.

Make sure the straps are tight and free from any twists, as this will provide the necessary stability and support.

Step 3: Attach the Hammock

Attach the hammock to the straps using carabiners or hooks. Ensure each hook or knot is securely fastened to prevent any slippage.

Hang the hammock so that it forms a gentle sag, with the lowest point being roughly 18 inches off the ground.

Step 4: Adjust for Comfort

Once the hammock is in place, test it by sitting in it carefully. Make any necessary adjustments to the height or tension of the ropes to achieve the desired level of comfort and support.

A slight diagonal lay will offer more back support and a flatter sleeping position.

Step 5: Add Sleeping Accessories

Place a sleeping pad or underquilt inside the hammock to provide insulation and comfort. If you anticipate colder weather, additional layers like an insulated blanket or sleeping bag can also be used to retain body heat.

Get Comfortable With Our Sleeping Pads

Step 6: Test Your Setup

Finally, lay down in the hammock to test your setup. Ensure it's comfortable and well-balanced, making any last-minute adjustments as needed.

Enjoy a peaceful night's sleep with the natural sway of your hammock amongst the great outdoors.

How to Set Up a Hammock With a Tarp Shelter

Sleeping under the stars in your hammock is beautiful during those warm summer evenings, but when the weather is more unpredictable or harsh, you need something more. That's where a tarp comes into it.

Adding a tarp to your hammock tent set-up is quick and simple with our step-by-step guide.

Step 1: Select the Right Tarp

Choose a tarp that is large enough to cover your hammock completely, ensuring protection from rain and wind.

Waterproof materials, such as ripstop nylon or polyester, are ideal for a reliable and durable shelter. A rectangular or hexagonal tarp provides ample coverage and versatility in setup.

What Size Tarp is Right for Your Trip?

Step 2: Position the Ridgeline

Run a ridgeline between the two trees or anchor points used for your hammock. Position it slightly above the height of your hammock straps.

Securely tie the ridgeline to ensure it can support the weight of the tarp and withstand environmental factors like wind.

Step 3: Attach the Tarp

Drape the tarp over the ridgeline, centring it to provide even coverage over your hammock. Secure the tarp's midpoint to the ridgeline, using guylines or clips to keep it in place.

Ensure the tarp spans adequately to protect the hammock from rain while allowing adequate airflow.

Step 4: Secure the Tarp Edges

Stake the corners of the tarp into the ground at a slight angle, using guylines for added tension and stability.

Adjust the positioning to create the desired tent-like shape. This not only keeps you dry but also allows water to run off the sides efficiently.

Shop Our Full Tarp Range Today!

Step 5: Ensure Proper Ventilation

To prevent condensation build-up inside your shelter, make sure there is adequate airflow.

Adjust the height of the tarp’s sides to allow for circulation without exposing your hammock to the elements. A slight gap between the tarp and the ground helps maintain this balance.

How to Choose the Right Hammock

Choosing the right hammock for your camping trip doesn’t have to be complicated – just think about a few key things.

First up, the material. Go for something durable and breathable, like parachute nylon, which is comfy and built to last. Then there’s size.

Hammocks come in all sorts of widths and lengths, from the DD Junior to the DD Frontline King Size, so pick one that feels roomy enough, especially if you like to sleep diagonally for extra support. 

Don’t forget about weight capacity – make sure it can handle you and any gear you might toss in.

The camping climate matters, too. If it’s chilly, look for a hammock that works with underquilts or double layers to keep you warm. For buggy spots, an integrated bug net will be your best friend.

Lastly, think about setup and portability. A lightweight, compact hammock is perfect if you’re hiking to your campsite or like to keep things simple.

With these tips in mind, you’ll be all set to pick a hammock that makes your camping trip even better. Happy hanging!

Shop Our Full Range of Hammocks

Our Hammock Camping Top Tips

Setting up your hammock properly is key to ensuring a comfortable and enjoyable camping trip, but it's not just about following the steps.

There are some other skills that are necessary to help you get hammock camping down to an art.

1. Learn How to Choose Appropriate Trees for Your Hammock Setup

Picking the right trees is key to staying safe and comfy and making the most of your hammock. Look for trees that are at least 6 inches thick – this means they’re strong enough to hold your hammock without getting damaged.

Take a good look at the trees to make sure they’re healthy. Check for strong roots, no signs of rot, and plenty of green leaves.

Stay away from trees with dead branches (aka widow-makers) that could drop unexpectedly, especially on windy days.

For the best tree hammock setup, find trees that are about 12 to 15 feet apart so your hammock hangs just right. Also, check the ground in between for any obstacles or hazards.

Lastly, think about the area around you. Look for trees that offer natural shade, and make sure you’re not disturbing a delicate ecosystem while setting up your camp.

2. Remember to Double Check Your Hammock Straps

Before you settle in for the night, take a moment to make sure your hammock straps are secured properly – it’s key for both your safety and comfort.

Loose straps can lead to unwelcome surprises, like your hammock slipping or even falling, and no one wants that in the middle of the night! 

Double-checking your setup ensures the straps are tight and free of twists or knots that could come loose over time. It’s especially important since things like temperature and humidity can mess with the tension. 

While you’re at it, take a quick look at the alignment. A properly set hammock isn’t just safer – it’s way more comfortable, so you can actually enjoy a good night’s sleep under the stars.

Plus, adjusting your straps can help protect your gear and the trees by evenly distributing the weight. A little extra effort now means a much better experience later!

3. Don't Forget Your Sleeping Pad

When preparing for your camping trip, don’t forget to pack a sleeping pad! It’s something a lot of people overlook, but it can make a huge difference in comfort and warmth.

Unlike a regular tent, a hammock leaves you hanging in the air, which means the wind can steal your body heat pretty quickly. A sleeping pad acts as a barrier against the cold and keeps you nice and warm.

Plus, it adds some extra cushioning and helps you stay comfortable all night. With a simple sleeping pad, your hammock camping trip can go from chilly and uncomfortable to warm and restful – a total game-changer for nights under the stars!

We've broken down our hiking checklist into what you need for basic hikes, day hikes, and extended hiking trips to help ensure you don't forget anything crucial for your next outdoor adventure.

Whether you're a hiking newbie or a forgetful, experienced adventurer, our checklist can make your hiking trip more enjoyable.

What to Take On a Hike: Basic Gear

As with any outside activity, you need some basic hiking kit no matter what kind of hike you're undertaking. Here are our key pieces of equipment to make hiking safe and comfortable.

1. A Suitable Backpack

A suitable backpack is essential for any hiking trip as it allows you to comfortably carry all your essentials, such as water, snacks, navigation tools, and extra clothing.

Ensuring that your backpack fits well and distributes weight evenly reduces strain on your body, allowing you to hike safely and efficiently.

A well-organised backpack also makes it easy to access your items, ensuring you are prepared for any situation along the trail.

For shorter hikes, the Mystery Ranch Urban Assault backpack is ideal for carrying your supplies for a few hours or even a full day if you're a smart packer. If you're undertaking a longer, multi-day hike, we'd recommend the Highlander Harrier Pack. With a 35L capacity, this rucksack holds everything you need.

Read More: Rucksack Buying Guide

2. An Appropriate Water Bottle

Staying hydrated is crucial during a hike, making an appropriate water bottle indispensable. A bottle that keeps water cool ensures refreshing hydration throughout your trek, enhancing performance and comfort.

Opt for a bottle with a sufficient capacity to meet your hydration needs without being overly heavy, as excessive weight can cause fatigue. Balancing capacity and weight allows you to trek efficiently without risking dehydration.

Choose a durable, leak-proof bottle to withstand trail challenges while maintaining easy accessibility.

For short and day hikes, the Camelbak Eddy+ is the ideal option. Holding a litre of water, it’ll keep you hydrated throughout your adventure. For extended hiking trails, the Easy Camp Folding Water Carrier is ideal for bringing water to your overnight camp. 

Just remember to use water purification methods for fresh water.

Stay Hydrated With Our Water Bottles

3. Comfortable Hiking Shoes

Comfortable and supportive hiking shoes are vital for hikes of any length to prevent blisters and protect your joints, enhancing both efficiency and enjoyment.

They provide essential support on uneven terrain, reducing the risk of ankle injuries.

Durable materials extend the life of the boots, ensuring they withstand various trail challenges while supporting your journey every step of the way.

Day Hiking Kit Checklist

If you're going on a day hike, you'll need to take more than what you'd take on a hike that lasts a few hours, but still less than you need for a multi-day hike.

All the things in our day hike packing list are in addition to the basic outdoor gear we mentioned above.

1. Torch & Headtorch

Even on a day hike, a torch and headtorch are essential for safety and unexpected delays. They ensure visibility when navigating through shaded or dense areas and provide crucial light if your hike extends into low light or evening hours.

In emergencies, these tools can help signal for assistance. Having a reliable light source prepares you for unforeseen changes in weather or terrain, contributing to a safe and stress-free hiking experience.

The Alonefire HP20 LED Headlight is a great all-rounder headtorch that's ideal for trekking after dark and pottering around camp. For a lightweight option for day hikes, we recommend the O Light Keychain Torch.

Shop Our Camping Lights

2. Phone & Power Bank

A phone is vital for communication, navigation, and emergency assistance. Combined with a power bank, you ensure your phone remains charged throughout the hike, maintaining access to maps and emergency contacts.

This duo is essential for safety, especially in unfamiliar or remote areas, as it allows you to stay connected and call for help if needed.

3. Lightweight Rain Jacket

A lightweight rain jacket is crucial on a day hike as weather conditions can change rapidly, exposing you to unexpected rain.

It provides waterproof protection while being easy to pack and carry without adding significant weight. The jacket's breathability helps regulate body temperature, keeping you comfortable during exertion.

We recommend the Highlander Halo Full Zip Tactical Jacket for day hikes.

4. Spare Insulation Layer

A spare insulating layer is essential for day hikes, particularly when climbing peaks, as temperatures can drop significantly at higher altitudes.

This layer helps retain body heat, safeguarding against hypothermia and ensuring comfort amid unpredictable mountain weather conditions.

Having an extra layer ready allows hikers to adjust to changing temperatures swiftly, enhancing safety and warmth during rest stops or in colder, windier summit conditions.

How to Keep Warm On a Budget

5. Eye Protection & Sunscreen

Even in winter, eye protection and sunscreen are essential for day hikes. Snow and ice can intensify UV exposure by reflecting sunlight, increasing the risk of sunburn and eye damage. 

Sunglasses safeguard your eyes from harmful rays and glare, while sunscreen protects exposed skin against harmful UV radiation. Prioritising these items can prevent sun-related harm.

We recommend using a general sunscreen like the Care Plus Outdoor & Sea SPF 50 and a lip sunscreen like the Sun Protection Lipstick to keep your lips and skin protected.

6. Map & Compass

A map and compass are crucial for day hikes as they provide reliable navigation, especially in areas with poor GPS signals or unexpected route changes. These traditional tools require no batteries, ensuring continuous and accurate use with strong map reading skills.

Understanding terrain features and pinpointing your location enhances safety, preventing disorientation and getting lost.

By planning and tracking routes, a map and compass enable hikers to navigate confidently through diverse terrains, ensuring a successful and stress-free adventure in nature.

What Size Tarp is Right for Your Trip?

3. Enough Food Provisions

On long-distance hikes, ensuring you have enough food provisions is crucial, particularly in cold or wet conditions where energy expenditure is high.

High-calorie, non-perishable foods are ideal, as they offer sustained energy and pack easily. By prioritising sufficient food supplies, hikers enhance their resilience and capacity to handle adverse weather conditions, ensuring safety and success on their adventures.

Stay Fuelled With Our Camp Meals

4. Sleeping Equipment

Sleeping equipment such as sleeping bags, mats, and pillows are crucial for ensuring proper rest during long-distance hikes. Sleeping bags provide insulation and warmth, essential for combating cold nights.

5. Comfortable Spare Socks

Comfortable spare socks are crucial on a long hike to keep your feet dry and blister-free, enhancing overall comfort and happiness. Wet feet can lead to blisters and trench foot, impacting hiking endurance and enjoyment.

Spare socks provide necessary warmth, absorb moisture, and ensure foot hygiene, which is essential for preventing infections.

By maintaining dry, comfortable feet, hikers can focus on the journey ahead, ensuring a pleasant and successful adventure in diverse weather conditions.

To avoid blisters, opt for socks with appropriate arch support and padding, like a mid-weight boot sock!

6. Suitable Trekking Poles

Suitable trekking poles are indispensable for comfortable hiking. They provide stability on uneven terrain and reduce strain on joints. They help distribute weight, alleviating pressure on knees and enhancing balance.

When pitching shelters, trekking poles serve as versatile supports, simplifying setup and adding structural stability.

Their multi-functionality makes them an essential addition to any hiking kit, ensuring comfort and efficiency in both trekking and shelter arrangements.

7. First Aid Kit & Survival Gear

First aid kits and survival gear are crucial for handling emergencies on long-distance hikes.

Quick access to these tools enhances preparedness, promotes safety, and minimises risk for you and your group when facing the unpredictable challenges of wilderness adventures.

8. Water Purification Methods

Water purification methods are essential for long-distance hikes, ensuring safe hydration from natural sources.

Techniques like filtration systems, purification tablets, or UV purifiers remove harmful pathogens and contaminants from water, preventing illnesses.

Carrying reliable purification options allows hikers to access clean water consistently, crucial for maintaining energy levels and overall health when exploring remote areas. Prioritising water safety is vital for sustaining endurance and ensuring a safe, enjoyable hiking experience.

title: Are Survival Knives Legal in the UK? What to Know for Your Camping Trip
author: Alex Newman
excerpt: Quick answer: Yes. Survival knives are legal to buy and own in the UK if you are 18 or over, but you need a good reason, such as camping or bushcraft, to carry one in public. Only a non-locking folding knife with a blade
html:
Quick answer: Yes. Survival knives are legal to buy and own in the UK if you are 18 or over, but you need a good reason, such as camping or bushcraft, to carry one in public. Only a non-locking folding knife with a blade under 3 inches (7.62cm) can be carried without a reason. Browse our bushcraft and survival knives.

Legal to own? Yes. You must be 18 or over to buy a knife
Carry without a reason Only non-locking folding knives with a blade under 3 inches (7.62cm)
Locking and fixed blades Need a good reason, such as camping or bushcraft; carry them packed away in a sheath
Axes and saws Treated like other bladed tools: see our axes, saws and tools and Whitby knives

Updated November 2026

While survival knives are legal in the UK, restrictions apply, including where and who can carry them. We’ve answered your question on whether survival knives are legal in the UK and provided some important information you need to know.

In This Guide:

  • What Defines a Survival Knife?
  • Carrying Knives & Weapons — Basic Laws

    • 2. Offensive Weapons Act 2019
    • 3. Recent Updates: Offensive Weapons Act (Amendment) 2023
  • What is Classed as a "Good Reason" Under UK Knife Law?
  • Guidelines for Camping & Outdoor Activities
  • Are Locking Knives & Fixed Blades Legal for Camping?
  • Are Axes, Saws, Machetes, & Other Outdoor Knives Legal?
    • Axes & Hatchets
    • Saws (Inc. Bushcraft & Folding Saws)
    • Machetes
  • What Should You Not Carry When Camping?
  • Practical Advice for Carrying & Using Outdoor Cutting Tools Legally
  • Conclusion: Using Camping Knives Within the UK
  • FAQs

We know just how useful survival knives can be when you're out in the wilderness. Whether you want to cut plants for kindling or bedding, or you're trying to open a can of food, a good survival knife can be invaluable.

But before you purchase one, it's important to understand the laws surrounding the possession and use of knives in the UK.

What Defines a Survival Knife?

A survival or bushcraft knife typically has a fixed blade with serrated edges and is designed for use in extreme outdoor situations. They usually range from 5-10 inches long and can come with additional features such as fire starters, compasses, or sharpeners.

Carrying Knives & Weapons — Basic Laws

In the United Kingdom, the law governing possession and use of knives falls under the Criminal Justice Act 1988 and the Offensive Weapons Act 2019.

Under these laws, it's illegal to carry a knife in public without a valid reason or lawful authority. The maximum penalty for carrying an offensive weapon is four years in prison.

A knife can be considered an offensive weapon if it's used to threaten, harm or injure someone, regardless of its design or size. It also includes any object adapted for causing injury.

1. Criminal Justice Act 1988, Section 139

The Criminal Justice Act 1988, Section 139 states that it's an offence to carry a bladed or pointed article in a public place without good reason or lawful authority.

This law also applies to knives kept for camping, fishing, or other outdoor activities.

2. Offensive Weapons Act 2019

The Offensive Weapons Act 2019 prohibits possession of certain dangerous weapons in public places. This includes zombie knives, knuckle dusters, and flick knives with blades over 3 inches long.

3. Recent Updates: Offensive Weapons Act (Amendment) 2023

In 2023, the government made some updates to the Offensive Weapons Act with the Offensive Weapons Act (Amendment) 2023. The amendment includes a ban on the possession of certain weapons, such as flick knives or gravity knives.

What is Classed as a "Good Reason" Under UK Knife Law?

Under UK knife law, a "good reason" for carrying a knife typically relates to lawful purposes where the possession of a blade is necessary or justified.

Examples of good reasons might include

  • Carrying a knife for work purposes, such as a tradesperson using a tool for their job
  • Recreational activities like camping or fishing where a knife is required for practical use
  • Carrying a blade as part of a national costume or for use in a legitimate display, demonstration, or collection

However, it is important to note that the burden of proof lies with the individual to demonstrate the necessity and legality of carrying the knife.

Guidelines for Camping & Outdoor Activities

When it comes to camping and outdoor activities, carrying a knife can be essential for practical tasks such as food preparation, cutting ropes, or crafting tools. However, it’s crucial to ensure that the knife you carry complies with the law.

Generally, folding knives with a blade length of less than 3 inches (7.62 cm) are permitted, provided they do not lock into place.

For larger knives, such as fixed-blade knives or a multi-tool knife, you must demonstrate a clear and legitimate reason for carrying them, such as forming part of an outdoor survival kit or specific camping needs.

It is important to always handle knives responsibly and store them securely during transport to avoid accidental harm or causing alarm to others.

Misuse of knives, even when intended for camping purposes, can lead to legal consequences.

Carrying your survival blade in a sheath is the ideal way to keep you and others safe while you travel to your camp location. Shop our range of knife sheaths online.

Are Locking Knives & Fixed Blades Legal for Camping?

In the UK, you can’t carry locking knives or fixed-blade knives in public without a good reason. Locking knives are folding knives that lock when open, and fixed-blade knives don’t fold at all.

Both are seen as more dangerous, so the rules are stricter. If you need to carry one, like for work, fishing, camping, or a specific reason, you’ll need to justify it if someone asks.

We recommend sticking to handy multi-tools to keep things legal and convenient. Shop our range online.

Are Axes, Saws, Machetes, & Other Outdoor Knives Legal?

There are many types of bladed articles that can be useful when camping, especially if you're wild camping or embarking on a longer survival adventure. So, what's the law surrounding larger blades that you might need for camping?

Axes & Hatchets

Axes and hatchets can be okay to carry in the UK for camping, but it really depends on the situation, your intent, and how you’re transporting them.

If you’re using an axe or hatchet for something legit, like chopping firewood while camping, that’s usually a reasonable excuse.

But carrying one around in public without a good reason could land you in trouble, as it might be seen as an offensive weapon.

To stay on the safe side, keep it securely stored — like in your car or backpack — and avoid carrying it openly where it might worry people.

If the authorities ask, just be ready to explain that you’re using it for a practical, lawful purpose related to your camping trip. Simple as that!

Shop Our Camping Axes

Saws (Inc. Bushcraft & Folding Saws)

When it comes to saws, like bushcraft or folding saws, the rules in the UK are pretty similar to those for axes or hatchets.

If you’re bringing a saw for camping, it’s usually fine as long as you have a good reason and use it sensibly.

For example, taking a folding saw to cut large wood logs at your campsite is generally seen as a valid excuse.

Browse Our Camping Saws Range

Machetes

In the UK, machetes are pretty tightly regulated because of their size and potential as a weapon.

Generally, we'd recommend steering clear of machetes as a camping tool. Not only could you get into trouble, but they're also impractical and cumbersome.

What Should You Not Carry When Camping?

Carrying items such as large knives, machetes, or other blades without a valid reason is strongly advised against.

Weapons like butterfly knives, flick knives, and disguised blades are outright illegal in the UK.

Carrying tools or blades in public for reasons unrelated to their intended use can land you in trouble with the law.

It's always best to stick to smaller bushcraft tools that are both practical and permissible for your outdoor activities.

Practical Advice for Carrying & Using Outdoor Cutting Tools Legally

When camping, carrying and using a survival knife legally requires careful consideration to ensure compliance with UK laws. Here are our practical tips for making carrying a camping knife to your camp less stressful!

  1. Always ensure the knife you bring is appropriate for camping activities, such as food preparation or cutting ropes, and
  2. Avoid carrying knives with locking mechanisms or fixed blades unless absolutely necessary
  3. Keep the knife stored securely when not in use, such as in your backpack or camping gear, rather than carrying it openly.
  4. Be prepared to explain its purpose clearly if questioned by authorities, emphasising its use for legitimate camping needs.
  5. Use the knife responsibly — avoid any actions that might be perceived as threatening or reckless

We also recommend always bringing a complete first aid kit with you when you’re using a survival knife in the wilderness. No matter how skilled you are, accidents can still happen, and it’s best to be prepared! 

Read More: Safety Tips for Using a Knife When Camping

Conclusion: Using Camping Knives Within the UK

Please note it is entirely your or the user's responsibility to ensure that any knives in your possession are used safely and legally while you’re camping within the UK. Always do your research and be aware of local laws and regulations regarding knife possession and usage. 

And remember, a knife is a tool, not a weapon. Use it responsibly and for its intended purpose to ensure a safe and enjoyable camping experience for yourself and others around you.

This article is a general guide and does not constitute legal advice. Always check local laws and regulations before purchasing or carrying any knives.

FAQs

Are Knives Legal for Bushcraft?

Yes, knives are legal for bushcraft in the UK if they comply with weapon laws. Ensure the knife is non-locking with a blade under three inches, and have a valid reason for carrying a larger, lockable blade.

Do Campers & Hikers Have Special Dispensation to Carry Camping Knives?

No, campers and hikers do not have special dispensation to carry camping knives. They must adhere to UK knife laws, ensuring the knife is appropriate, legal, and its use justifiable, such as for outdoor activities or survival purposes.

What Type of Knife is Best For Camping?

A fixed-blade knife is best for camping due to its durability and versatility. It should have a comfortable grip and be suitable for tasks like food preparation, wood carving, and fire starting. However, you still need to ensure it complies with local laws.

What Can Knives Be Used for When Camping?

Knives can be used for a variety of camping tasks, including food preparation, cutting rope or cord, carving, fire starting, and other survival activities.

Always check the knife is suitable for these tasks and complies with local regulations before heading out.

Can You Use a Knife for Camping Under 18?

In the UK, individuals under 18 can use a knife for camping if supervised by an adult.

Ensure the knife is legal and appropriate for camping tasks, and always follow local laws and guidelines regarding knife use. Anyone under 18 shouldn’t be carrying a knife to the campsite and cannot legally purchase a knife.

Rule 101 of camping — don’t neglect your hygiene (especially if you’re on a trip with your pals!). Our camping bathing guide is full of tips and tricks for staying fresh and clean between your adventures, along with our favourite products to throw in your backpack.

While some campsites have full shower facilities (some even with hot water…imagine that!), it's not always the case, and you can't guarantee access to running water at your camp. So, what should you do?

We've picked up a few tips and tricks over the years that have come in handy for staying clean while camping, including taking nifty hygiene products (like the BCB Folding Toothbrush), and even portable showers (the BCB Solar Shower has definitely saved us a few times). 

But sometimes, you just need to get creative with what you have on hand. Read on for our full guide to camping bathing…

Our Top Camping Hygiene Tips

If you're not camping somewhere with a shower block, it doesn't mean you have to go without soap for the duration of your trip. Here’s how to shower when camping with our top tips to stay hygienic and feel fresh during your trip.

Taking Care Of Oral Hygiene

Keeping your teeth clean while camping isn’t just about fresh breath — it’s also about avoiding cavities and gum problems.

A quick routine of brushing twice a day with a travel toothbrush, like the BCB Folding Toothbrush, and a small tube of toothpaste can go a long way. Try using biodegradable toothpaste to keep things eco-friendly, and don’t forget to dispose of wastewater properly.

If water’s hard to come by, sugar-free gum can help keep your mouth feeling fresh.

Taking care of your oral hygiene means you can enjoy your camping trip without any discomfort or surprises!

Shop Oral Hygiene Products

Portable Camp Showers

Portable camp showers are a game-changer for staying clean and refreshed on your outdoor adventures. They’re super easy to use — just fill up the reservoir, and you’re good to go with the attached hose or nozzle.

One of our favourites is the solar shower, like the BCB Solar Shower. It’s basically a heat-absorbing bag that warms up the water using sunlight, so you can enjoy a warm rinse even when it’s chilly out. Perfect, right?

These showers are a lifesaver after muddy hikes, dips in the lake, or any time you’re a little too covered in the great outdoors. 

Plus, they’re a must-have for keeping up with hygiene on longer camping trips when there’s no access to regular facilities. Stay fresh and keep adventuring!

Waterless Hygiene Products


Adding waterless hygiene products to your camping gear is a game-changer for staying clean and fresh when running water isn’t an option.

Perfect for camping, hiking, or any outdoor adventure, these handy products let you skip the rinse but still feel great. Towel-off body washes, and shampoos make it easy — just apply, wipe off with a towel, and you’re good to go.

Dry shampoo is another lifesaver, soaking up oil and refreshing your hair without the hassle of washing.

Whether you’re wild camping in the wilderness or just don't want to queue for festival showers, these products help you stay comfortable and clean, no matter where your adventures take you!

Shop Waterless Hygiene Products

How to Warm Up After Outdoor Camp Showers

After stepping out of an outdoor camp shower, warming up quickly is key to staying comfy and avoiding a chill.

One of the best ways to do this? Cosy up by the campfire. The heat from the flames not only dries you off but gives you a relaxing moment to unwind after your wash.

On colder nights, rechargeable hand warmers, like the Ocoopa UT2s Rechargeable Hand Warmer, are a game-changer. Just pop them into your pockets or hold them for an instant heat boost.

A hot water bottle works wonders, too. Keep it close, or tuck it under a blanket for some extra warmth. And don’t forget to throw on fresh, dry clothes right after your shower; warm socks and a snug jumper will keep you feeling toasty.


How to Stay Dry While Camping

Why Is It Important to Maintain Personal Hygiene When Camping?

Keeping clean while camping is super important for both your health and comfort.

Start with your tent and sleeping bag — keeping them clean can prevent dirt, sweat, and bacteria from building up, which means no bad smells (your campmates will be more than glad about that one) or skin irritation.

A quick shake-out of your sleeping bag and air out your tent regularly can make a big difference, especially if it’s been damp.

Don’t forget about yourself, too! Wiping down with biodegradable wet wipes or rinsing off in clean water is an easy way to stay fresh and avoid clogged pores or skin issues.

And watch out for your feet. Wearing damp socks or shoes for too long can lead to fungal infections, which no one wants on a camping trip.

A little effort goes a long way. Staying clean will help you feel better and make sure your camping adventure stays fun and hassle-free!

How to Stay Eco-Friendly While Showering When Camping

Showering outside while camping can be a great experience, but it’s important to keep it eco-friendly.

  1. Use biodegradable soaps and shampoos that won’t harm plants, animals, or water sources.
  2. To avoid contaminating the water, set up your shower at least 200 feet (about 60 metres) away from streams, rivers, or lakes.
  3. To save water, try using a shower with a controlled flow or a simple bucket system. 
  4. If you’re camping in a sensitive area, collect your wastewater in a container and dump it at a designated greywater spot if one is nearby.
  5. Be careful where the runoff goes; try not to let it flow onto plants that could get damaged.
Get Clean With JustSupplies

FAQs

How Do You Wash Your Body While Camping?

You can wash your body while camping by using biodegradable soap and water from a portable shower or a clean water source. Ensure you wash at least 200 feet from water bodies to protect the environment.

What is the Most Sanitary Way to Wash Your Body When Camping?

The most sanitary way to wash your body when camping is to use biodegradable soap with a portable shower or clean water and a washcloth. Always maintain a distance of 200 feet from natural water sources to prevent contamination.

Is it OK to Skip Showering When Camping?

Yes, it is fine to skip showering when camping if necessary — but not personal hygiene altogether.

Prioritise hygiene by using wet wipes or a washcloth to clean essential areas and stay comfortable. Always follow eco-friendly practices to minimise your impact on the environment.

Are Campsite Showers Hygienic?

Yes, campsite showers can be hygienic if they are regularly maintained and cleaned. Always bring flip-flops and personal supplies like soap and a towel to ensure cleanliness and minimise the risk of infections while using shared facilities.

  • Propane/Isobutane

  • And alcohol-based fuels

The one you’ll need will depend on a couple of factors, the most important three being,

  1. The type of camping stove you have
  2. The temperature and conditions you’ll be camping in
  3. The duration of your trip

Best Camping Fuel Stove Recommendations

Most Popular Types of Camping Fuel

There are a few types of camping fuel that outdoor enthusiasts come back to time and time again. These fuels are either easy to come by in camping stores or useful in common camping environments.

Here are the most popular types of camping fuel for UK adventures.

Propane Fuel

Propane fuel is super popular for camping trips. It’s efficient and convenient and comes in sturdy canisters or tanks that are a breeze to carry and use.

Propane also works great in all kinds of weather — even in colder climates where other fuels might let you down. That’s why it’s a favourite for year-round campers.

Most portable camping stoves are designed to hook up directly to the canister or use a hose adapter, making them simple to set up.

These stoves give you steady, adjustable heat, so whether you’re whipping up a quick snack or cooking something fancier, propane’s got you covered in the great outdoors.

Butane Fuel

What we recommend…

Shop now

Butane gas fuel is a favourite for camping stoves, and it’s easy to see why. It’s lightweight, portable, and super convenient for campsite cooking. Stored in pressurised canisters, it’s perfect for quick and easy use. 

Butane works best in mild to moderate weather, though — it can struggle in really cold temperatures because of its lower vaporisation point.

Stoves that run on butane are usually compact and great for short trips, which makes them a top pick for backpackers and casual campers. Plus, they’re super easy to use — just attach the canister, and you're good to go!

Isobutane Fuel

What we recommend…
